5 FORMS | 558 ATTACKS | 45 SILENT PROMPTS
CAGED as a practical chord, triad, root, arpeggio, and nearby-scale map
CAGED is used here as an indexing system, not a shape religion. Each form identifies a root region, a practical chord fragment, nearby triad inversions, a chord-tone arpeggio, and
surrounding scale tones. Full C and G forms are optional; partial voicings and triads are the primary performance material.
1. Find the roots 2. Extract the useful fragment 3. Connect chord, triad, and scale
Locate the form from its root strings before forming any Choose the smallest voicing that contains the required Use the local triad as the bridge between the full form,
grip. chord tones and register. arpeggio, and nearby scale tones.

Boundary and session protocol
Form the root map silently. Sound the practical fragment. Identify one triad inversion. Arpeggiate the chord tones. Add nearby scale tones and return to the chord. Do not force the full G form or a full
movable C form when a partial voicing is cleaner and more musical.
SUCCESS The player can move from a root to a useful chord, triad, arpeggio, and scale phrase without searching the entire neck.
Standard tuning. CAGED is used as a practical root, chord, triad, arpeggio, and nearby-scale index. Page 1 of 20

guidance_lines.text: SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION II, LEVEL 16
MAJOR SCALE FOUR-NOTE ROLLING SEQUENCE - ONE-OCTAVE NECK LADDER: A TO A
PURPOSE
Turn the compact one-octave major scale into overlapping four-note groups. Complete the full
40-note up/down rolling cell, release pressure, move the entire hand-and-thumb frame exactly
one fret, and repeat through every major key. Begin with A major at low-E fret 5, climb to
A major at fret 17, then reverse and return one fret at a time.
WHY THIS LEVEL RETURNS TO ONE OCTAVE
Level 15 expanded the three-note sequence across two octaves and all six strings. Level 16
deliberately returns to the compact three-string octave so the new four-note overlap can be
learned without simultaneously managing the upper-octave B-string offset. Level 17 can extend
this exact sequence across the complete two-octave frame.
IMPORTANT INTERPRETATION
Moving one fixed scale shape by one fret transposes it. A major is the starting rung, not the
key of every rung. A fixed-key A-major exercise in every neck position requires changing the
note layout and remains a separate branch.
MAJOR-SCALE FORMULA
Degrees: 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8
Intervals: whole - whole - half - whole - whole - whole - half
COMPACT ONE-OCTAVE SHAPE - ROOT FRET R ON LOW E
Low E string: R, R+2               Fingers 2,4
A string:     R-1, R, R+2          Fingers 1,2,4
D string:     R-1, R+1, R+2        Fingers 1,3,4
The four-fret hand frame runs from R-1 through R+2.
ROLLING FOUR-NOTE SEQUENCE
Each new group begins one scale degree farther along. At each group boundary, the line drops
a diatonic third and then continues forward. Three notes overlap from one group to the next.
Do not pause, accent, or reset at a group boundary.
CELL AND PICKING RULE
The complete up/down cell contains 10 groups and 40 notes. The octave root is repeated at the
turn: the last note of 5-6-7-8 is followed by the first note of 8-7-6-5. Because 40 is even,
the next key begins with the same pick orientation. Because every group has four notes, every
group also begins with the same stroke.
D-start groups: D-U-D-U | D-U-D-U | D-U-D-U ... through all 10 groups.
U-start groups: U-D-U-D | U-D-U-D | U-D-U-D ... through all 10 groups.
Never restart the pick cycle at a new group, string crossing, scale turn, or one-fret shift.
NECK ROUTE
PRACTICE RULE
Use sixteenth notes: one four-note group per beat. Begin at roughly 75 percent of your clean
Level 15 metronome setting; for example, if Level 15 is clean at 80 BPM, begin near 60 BPM.
Master the A-major cell alone, then use 2-3 neighboring rungs and pause one beat after each
40-note cell. During the pause, release pressure and move the complete frame one fret. Repeat
with both pick starts. Then remove the pause, connect the ladder, reverse at fret 17, and return
to fret 5. Add 2 BPM after three clean round trips. Reduce 4-6 BPM after two errors, an uneven
group pulse, dragged shift noise, a crossing accent, or rising tension. Advance after the full
route is clean with both pick starts on two separate days.

guidance_lines.text: SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION II, LEVEL 17
MAJOR SCALE FOUR-NOTE ROLLING SEQUENCE - TWO-OCTAVE SIX-STRING NECK LADDER: A TO A
PURPOSE
Extend the Level 16 four-note rolling sequence across the complete two-octave, six-string
major-scale frame. Complete the 96-note up/down cell, release pressure, move the entire
hand-and-thumb frame exactly one fret, and repeat through every major key. Begin with A major
at low-E fret 5, climb to A major at fret 17, then reverse and return one fret at a time.
WHAT CHANGES FROM LEVEL 16
Level 16 taught the four-note overlap inside the compact one-octave frame. Level 17 keeps the
same overlap and extends it through positions 1-15 across all six strings. This adds the middle
octave, additional string crossings, the B-string tuning offset, and a longer uninterrupted
pick cycle without changing the underlying four-note sequence rule.
IMPORTANT INTERPRETATION
Moving one fixed scale shape by one fret transposes it. A major is the starting rung, not the
key of every rung. The route passes through all 12 major keys before reaching A one octave
higher on the neck.
MAJOR-SCALE FORMULA
Intervals: whole - whole - half - whole - whole - whole - half, repeated through two octaves
TWO-OCTAVE SIX-STRING SHAPE - ROOT FRET R ON LOW E
Low E string: R, R+2               Fingers 2,4                 Degrees 1,2
A string:     R-1, R, R+2          Fingers 1,2,4               Degrees 3,4,5
D string:     R-1, R+1, R+2        Fingers 1,3,4               Degrees 6,7,8
G string:     R-1, R+1, R+2        Fingers 1,3,4               Degrees 9,10,11
B string:     R, R+2               Fingers 2,4                 Degrees 12,13
High e:       R-1, R               Fingers 1,2                 Degrees 14,15
The four-fret hand frame runs from R-1 through R+2.
ROLLING FOUR-NOTE SEQUENCE
ASCENDING:
DESCENDING:
Each new group begins one scale degree farther along. Three notes overlap from one group to
the next. At the boundary, the line drops a diatonic third and resumes forward motion. Do not
pause, accent, or reset at a group boundary.
CELL AND PICKING RULE
The complete up/down cell contains 24 groups and 96 notes. The high root is repeated at the
turn: the last note of 12-13-14-15 is followed by the first note of 15-14-13-12. Because 96
is even, the next key begins with the same pick orientation. Because each group has four notes,
every group also begins with the same stroke.
D-start groups: D-U-D-U | D-U-D-U | D-U-D-U ... through all 24 groups.
U-start groups: U-D-U-D | U-D-U-D | U-D-U-D ... through all 24 groups.
Never restart the pick cycle at a group, string crossing, octave root, turnaround, or frame shift.
NECK ROUTE
PRACTICE RULE
Use sixteenth notes: one four-note group per beat. Begin 15-20 BPM below your clean Level 16
tempo. Master the ascending and descending A-major halves separately, then link them through
the repeated high-root turn. Use 2-3 neighboring rungs and pause one beat after each 96-note
cell. During the pause, release pressure and move the complete frame one fret. Repeat with both
pick starts. Then remove the pause, connect the ladder, reverse at fret 17, and return to fret 5.
Add 2 BPM after three clean round trips. Reduce 4-6 BPM after two errors, an uneven group pulse,
dragged shift noise, a crossing accent, a B-string geometry error, or rising tension. Advance
after the full route is clean with both pick starts on two separate days.

guidance_lines.text: SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION II, LEVEL 18
MAJOR SCALE DIATONIC THIRDS - TWO-OCTAVE SIX-STRING NECK LADDER
PURPOSE
Level 18 leaves stepwise scale motion and begins intervallic sequencing. Each pair skips one scale degree:
1-3, 2-4, 3-5, and onward. After each upper note, the next pair rolls back one degree and continues upward.
The complete exercise retains the same two-octave six-string major-scale shape and one-fret chromatic neck route
used in Levels 13, 15, and 17.
MAIN SEQUENCE
INTERVAL-QUALITY PATTERN
Ascending:  M3 | m3 | m3 | M3 | M3 | m3 | m3 | M3 | m3 | m3 | M3 | M3 | m3
Each pair is either a major third (M3 = 4 semitones) or minor third (m3 = 3 semitones).
The quality is determined by the major key, not by a fixed fret shape.
CELL DESIGN
- 13 ascending pairs / 26 notes
- repeat the high root at the turnaround
- 13 descending pairs / 26 notes
- 52 notes total per key
- shift the entire hand-and-thumb frame one fret only after the final 3-1 pair
PICKING
Downstroke start: D-U | D-U | D-U | ... through all 26 pairs.
Upstroke start:   U-D | U-D | U-D | ... through all 26 pairs.
Because every pair and the complete 52-note cell are even, every pair and every new key begins on the same
pick orientation. Do not reset at string changes, the middle octave, the repeated high root, or a new key.
RHYTHM
Learning pulse: one pair per beat as eighth notes.
Performance pulse: two pairs per beat as straight sixteenth notes.
Accent the first note of each pair while learning, then remove the accents and equalize all notes.
PRACTICE PROGRESSION
1. A major, first octave only: pairs 1-3 through 6-8, then reverse.
2. A major, all 13 ascending pairs.
3. A major, all 13 descending pairs.
4. Link the 52-note cell; articulate both high-root notes without resetting.
5. Use two or three neighboring keys with a one-beat pause only after each complete cell.
6. Remove the pause and complete the entire route with both pick starts.
CHROMATIC ROUTE
Up:   A -> Bb -> B -> C -> Db -> D -> Eb -> E -> F -> Gb -> G -> Ab -> A
Down: Ab -> G -> Gb -> F -> E -> Eb -> D -> Db -> C -> B -> Bb -> A
Do not replay the high A-major rung during the down pass unless beginning a new round.

guidance_lines.text: SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION II, LEVEL 19
MAJOR SCALE DIATONIC TRIADS - TWO-OCTAVE SIX-STRING NECK LADDER
PURPOSE
Level 19 stacks one more scale tone onto the diatonic-thirds idea from Level 18. Every group now plays
a root, third, and fifth: 1-3-5, 2-4-6, 3-5-7, and onward. The exercise converts the major scale into
a connected chain of broken triads while retaining the same two-octave six-string shape and one-fret route.
MAIN SEQUENCE
HARMONIC FUNCTION AND QUALITY
Ascending:  I major | ii minor | iii minor | IV major | V major | vi minor | vii diminished | I major | ii minor | iii minor | IV major
Descending: IV major | iii minor | ii minor | I major | vii diminished | vi minor | V major | IV major | iii minor | ii minor | I major
CELL DESIGN
- 11 ascending triads / 33 notes
- repeat the high root at the turnaround as the first note of the descending line
- 11 descending triads / 33 notes
- 22 triads / 66 notes total per key
- shift the entire hand-and-thumb frame one fret only after the final 5-3-1 triad
PICKING
Downstroke start: D-U-D | U-D-U | D-U-D | U-D-U ... through all 22 triads.
Upstroke start:   U-D-U | D-U-D | U-D-U | D-U-D ... through all 22 triads.
Every three-note triad flips the starting stroke of the next triad. The complete 66-note cell is even,
so every new key begins on the same pick orientation. Do not reset at group boundaries, string changes,
the middle octave, the repeated high root, or a new key.
RHYTHM
Learning pulse: one triad per beat as eighth-note triplets.
Performance pulse: two triads per beat as sixteenth-note triplets (sextuplets).
Accent the root of each triad while learning, then remove the accents and equalize every note.
PRACTICE PROGRESSION
1. A major, first octave only: 1-3-5 through 4-6-8, then reverse.
2. A major, all 11 ascending triads.
3. A major, all 11 descending triads.
4. Link the 66-note cell; articulate both high-root notes without resetting.
5. Use two or three neighboring keys with a one-beat pause only after each complete cell.
6. Remove the pause and complete the entire route with both pick starts.
CHROMATIC ROUTE
Up:   A -> Bb -> B -> C -> Db -> D -> Eb -> E -> F -> Gb -> G -> Ab -> A
Down: Ab -> G -> Gb -> F -> E -> Eb -> D -> Db -> C -> B -> Bb -> A
Do not replay the high A-major rung during the down pass unless beginning a new round.
ROUTE REFERENCE

guidance_lines.text: SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION II, LEVEL 20
MAJOR SCALE SYNTHESIS CIRCUIT - TWO-OCTAVE SIX-STRING NECK LADDER
PURPOSE
Level 20 combines the established two-octave movements from Levels 13, 15, 17, 18, and 19 into
one uninterrupted major-scale circuit. Complete all five modules in the same key before shifting the
entire hand-and-thumb frame one fret. The low root is re-articulated at every module boundary.
FIVE-MODULE CELL
A. Linear scale:          30 notes - low root to high root, repeat high root, return to low root
B. Three-note roll:       78 notes - 13 ascending triplets and 13 descending triplets
C. Four-note roll:        96 notes - 12 ascending groups and 12 descending groups
D. Diatonic thirds:       52 notes - 13 ascending pairs and 13 descending pairs
E. Diatonic triads:       66 notes - 11 ascending triads and 11 descending triads
TOTAL:                   322 notes per key
MODULE ORDER
Linear -> Three-note roll -> Four-note roll -> Diatonic thirds -> Diatonic triads -> shift one fret
PICKING
All five module counts are even. With a downstroke start, every module and every new key begins on a
downstroke; with an upstroke start, each begins on an upstroke. Do not reset at group boundaries, string
changes, octave turns, module boundaries, or one-fret shifts.
RHYTHM
Learning mode: one note per metronome click through the complete circuit.
Native-pulse mode:
- Linear scale: 30 eighth notes = 15 beats
- Three-note roll: 78 triplet eighths = 26 beats
- Four-note roll: 96 sixteenth notes = 24 beats
- Diatonic thirds: 52 eighth notes = 26 beats
- Diatonic triads: 66 triplet eighths = 22 beats
TOTAL: 113 quarter-note beats per 322-note circuit
PRACTICE PROGRESSION
1. Learn each module separately in A major.
2. Link adjacent module pairs: A-B, B-C, C-D, and D-E.
3. Play the complete A-major circuit with a short pause at each boundary.
4. Remove the pauses while retaining a light accent on each new module root.
5. Remove the accents and use two or three neighboring keys.
6. Complete longer route sections with both a downstroke and an upstroke start.
CHROMATIC ROUTE
Up:   A -> Bb -> B -> C -> Db -> D -> Eb -> E -> F -> Gb -> G -> Ab -> A
Down: Ab -> G -> Gb -> F -> E -> Eb -> D -> Db -> C -> B -> Bb -> A
Do not replay the high A-major rung during the down pass unless beginning a new round.
ROUTE COUNT
25 circuits x 322 notes = 8,050 picked notes.
25 circuits x 113 native-pulse beats = 2,825 quarter-note beats.
The full route is a capstone endurance test, not a required daily warm-up.

guidance_lines.text: SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION III, LEVEL 21
NATURAL MINOR ONE-FRET NECK LADDER: A TO A
PURPOSE
Learn one compact one-octave natural-minor shape, move the complete hand-and-thumb frame exactly one fret,
and repeat through every natural-minor key. Begin with A natural minor at low-E fret 5, climb to A natural
minor at fret 17, then reverse and return one fret at a time.
PARALLEL MAJOR VS NATURAL MINOR
A major:         A B C# D E F# G# A
A natural minor: A B C  D E F  G  A
The 3rd, 6th, and 7th are each lowered one fret: 3 -> b3, 6 -> b6, 7 -> b7.
NATURAL-MINOR FORMULA
Degrees:   1 2 b3 4 5 b6 b7 8
Intervals: whole - half - whole - whole - half - whole - whole
COMPACT ONE-OCTAVE SHAPE - ROOT FRET R ON LOW E
Low E string: R, R+2, R+3          Fingers 1,3,4
A string:     R, R+2, R+3          Fingers 1,3,4
D string:     R, R+2               Fingers 1,3
The four-fret hand frame runs from R through R+3.
Ascending notes per string: 3-3-2. Descending notes per string: 2-3-3.
CELL AND PICKING RULE
Play degrees 1-2-b3-4-5-b6-b7-8, then 8-b7-b6-5-4-b3-2-1. The octave root is repeated at the turn.
This creates 16 notes, so the next key begins with the same alternate-picking orientation.
D-start: D U D U D U D U | D U D U D U D U
U-start: U D U D U D U D | U D U D U D U D
Do not restart the pick cycle at the scale turn or at the one-fret shift.
NECK ROUTE
PRACTICE RULE
First compare A major and A natural minor and identify the lowered 3rd, 6th, and 7th. Then use 3-4
neighboring natural-minor rungs. Play even eighth notes and pause one beat after each 16-note cell.
During the pause, release pressure and move the complete frame one fret. Repeat with both pick starts.
Then remove the pause, connect the ladder, reverse at fret 17, and return to fret 5.
Add 2 BPM after three clean round trips. Reduce 4-6 BPM after two errors, dragged shift noise, or rising tension.
Advance after the complete route is clean with both pick starts on two separate days.

guidance_lines.text: SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION III, LEVEL 22
NATURAL MINOR TWO-OCTAVE SIX-STRING NECK LADDER: A TO A
PURPOSE
Extend the Level 21 natural-minor shape across all six strings and two full octaves. Play the
complete 30-note up/down cell, release pressure, move the entire hand-and-thumb frame exactly one fret,
and repeat through every natural-minor key. Begin with A natural minor at low-E fret 5, climb to A
natural minor at fret 17, then reverse and return one fret at a time.
IMPORTANT INTERPRETATION
Moving one fixed scale shape by one fret transposes it. A natural minor is the starting rung, not the key
of every rung. A fixed-key A-minor exercise in every neck position requires changing the note layout and
remains a separate later branch.
NATURAL-MINOR FORMULA
Degrees:   1 2 b3 4 5 b6 b7, repeated in the second octave
Intervals: whole - half - whole - whole - half - whole - whole
TWO-OCTAVE SHAPE - ROOT FRET R ON LOW E
Low E string: R, R+2, R+3          Fingers 1,3,4
A string:     R, R+2, R+3          Fingers 1,3,4
D string:     R, R+2               Fingers 1,3
G string:     R-1, R, R+2          Fingers 1,2,4
B string:     R, R+1, R+3          Fingers 1,2,4
High e string:R                     Finger 1
The complete map spans R-1 through R+3. Do not hold a static five-fret stretch. Keep the lower-string
frame relaxed, release pressure for the one-fret G-string backreach, and rebuild the hand for the B string.
STRING-DISTRIBUTION RULE
Ascending note counts by string: 3 - 3 - 2 - 3 - 3 - 1.
Descending note counts by string: 1 - 3 - 3 - 2 - 3 - 3.
The G string begins one fret below the root reference, and the B-string tuning offset changes the visible
pattern again. Use the assigned fingering rather than copying one string pattern onto the next.
CELL AND PICKING RULE
Ascend from the low root through the middle octave to the high root, repeat the high root at the turn,
then descend to the low root. The result is 30 notes, so the next key begins with the same pick orientation.
D-start: strict D-U alternate picking through every string crossing, the turn, and the one-fret relocation.
U-start: strict U-D alternate picking through every string crossing, the turn, and the one-fret relocation.
Do not restart the pick cycle on a new string, at either octave, at the scale turn, or after shifting one fret.
NECK ROUTE
PRACTICE RULE
Begin 10-15 BPM below your clean Level 21 tempo. First master the A-natural-minor cell alone. Then use
2-3 neighboring rungs, play even eighth notes, and pause one beat after each 30-note cell while moving
the complete frame one fret. Repeat with both pick starts. Remove the pause, connect the ladder, reverse
at fret 17, and return to fret 5. Add 2 BPM after three clean round trips. Reduce 4-6 BPM after two errors,
string-crossing noise, dragged backreaches, or rising tension. Advance after the full route is clean with
both pick starts on two separate days.

36-note up/down rolling cell, release pressure, move the entire hand-and-thumb frame exactly one fret,
and repeat through every natural-minor key. Begin with A natural minor at low-E fret 5, climb to A natural
minor at fret 17, then reverse and return one fret at a time.

Level 22 expanded the straight natural-minor scale across two octaves and all six strings. Level 23
deliberately returns to the compact three-string octave so the new overlap pattern can be learned without
also managing the upper-octave backreach and B-string offset. Level 24 will extend the sequence later.
IMPORTANT INTERPRETATION
Moving one fixed scale shape by one fret transposes it. A natural minor is the starting rung, not the key of every rung.
A fixed-key A-natural-minor exercise in every neck position requires changing the note layout and remains a separate branch.
NATURAL-MINOR FORMULA
Degrees:   1 2 b3 4 5 b6 b7 8
Intervals: whole - half - whole - whole - half - whole - whole
COMPACT ONE-OCTAVE SHAPE - ROOT FRET R ON LOW E
Low E string: R, R+2, R+3          Fingers 1,3,4
A string:     R, R+2, R+3          Fingers 1,3,4
D string:     R, R+2               Fingers 1,3
The four-fret hand frame runs from R through R+3.
Ascending notes per string: 3-3-2. Descending notes per string: 2-3-3.
ROLLING THREE-NOTE SEQUENCE
Each new triplet starts one scale degree farther along. Between groups, the line rolls back one degree.
Do not pause or reset at a triplet boundary, even when the string crossing moves from late to early.

UP:   EEE | EEA | EAA | AAA | AAD | ADD
DOWN: DDA | DAA | AAA | AAE | AEE | EEE
The all-one-string groups alternate with late and early crossings. Keep the landing note equal in volume.

The complete up/down cell contains 12 triplets and 36 notes. The octave root is repeated at the turn:
the last note of b6-b7-8 is followed by the first note of 8-b7-b6. Because 36 is even, the next key
begins with the same pick orientation.
D-start groups: D-U-D | U-D-U | D-U-D | U-D-U ...
U-start groups: U-D-U | D-U-D | U-D-U | D-U-D ...
Do not restart the pick cycle at a new triplet, string crossing, scale turn, or one-fret relocation.
NECK ROUTE
PRACTICE RULE
Use eighth-note triplets: one three-note group per beat. Begin 12-18 BPM below your clean Level 22 tempo.
Master the A-natural-minor cell alone, then use 2-3 neighboring rungs and pause one beat after each 36-note cell.
During the pause, release pressure and move the complete frame one fret. Repeat with both pick starts.
Then remove the pause, connect the ladder, reverse at fret 17, and return to fret 5.
Add 2 BPM after three clean round trips. Reduce 4-6 BPM after two errors, broken triplet pulse, dragged shift
noise, or rising tension. Advance after the complete route is clean with both pick starts on two separate days.

guidance_lines.text: SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION III, LEVEL 24
NATURAL MINOR THREE-NOTE ROLLING SEQUENCE - TWO-OCTAVE SIX-STRING NECK LADDER: A TO A
PURPOSE
Carry the Level 23 overlapping three-note sequence across the complete two-octave natural-minor frame
from Level 22. Complete the 78-note up/down rolling cell, release pressure, move the entire hand-and-thumb
frame exactly one fret, and repeat through every natural-minor key. Begin with A natural minor at low-E
fret 5, climb to A natural minor at fret 17, then reverse and return one fret at a time.
WHAT CHANGES FROM LEVEL 23
Level 23 isolated the rolling motion inside one octave. Level 24 preserves the same three-note overlap but
extends it through positions 1-15 and all six strings. The new work is not a new sequence formula; it is
maintaining that formula through the middle octave, the G-string backreach, the B-string tuning offset,
the single high-e endpoint, the repeated high root, and the one-fret relocation.
IMPORTANT INTERPRETATION
Moving one fixed scale shape by one fret transposes it. A natural minor is the starting rung, not the key
of every rung. A fixed-key A-natural-minor exercise in every neck position requires changing the note layout
and remains a separate later branch.
NATURAL-MINOR FORMULA
One octave: 1 2 b3 4 5 b6 b7 8
Two octaves: 1 2 b3 4 5 b6 b7 8 9 b10 11 12 b13 b14 15
Intervals: whole - half - whole - whole - half - whole - whole, then repeat
The tablature uses a Pos row for scale positions 1-15; the degree map above identifies the altered tones.
TWO-OCTAVE SHAPE - ROOT FRET R ON LOW E
Low E string: R, R+2, R+3          Fingers 1,3,4
A string:     R, R+2, R+3          Fingers 1,3,4
D string:     R, R+2               Fingers 1,3
G string:     R-1, R, R+2          Fingers 1,2,4
B string:     R, R+1, R+3          Fingers 1,2,4
High e string:R                     Finger 1
The complete map spans R-1 through R+3. Do not hold a static five-fret stretch. Release and rebuild the
frame for the G-string backreach and again for the B-string offset.
ROLLING THREE-NOTE SEQUENCE
Each new triplet begins one scale position farther along. The line moves forward while briefly revisiting
the previous two positions. Do not pause or reset at a triplet boundary.
STRING-CROSSING MAP
UP:   EEE | EEA | EAA | AAA | AAD | ADD | DDG | DGG | GGG | GGB | GBB | BBB | BBe
DOWN: eBB | BBB | BBG | BGG | GGG | GGD | GDD | DDA | DAA | AAA | AAE | AEE | EEE
The route includes no-crossing groups, early crossings, and late crossings. Keep every landing inside the
same triplet pulse, especially at D-to-G and G-to-B where the visible fret geometry changes.
CELL AND PICKING RULE
The complete cell contains 13 ascending triplets and 13 descending triplets: 26 groups and 78 notes.
The final high root of the ascent is immediately followed by the same high root to begin the descent.
Because each triplet is odd, the starting stroke alternates from group to group. Because the complete
78-note cell is even, the next key begins with the original pick orientation.
D-start groups: D-U-D | U-D-U | D-U-D | U-D-U ...
U-start groups: U-D-U | D-U-D | U-D-U | D-U-D ...
Do not restart at a triplet, string crossing, middle octave, repeated high root, or one-fret shift.
NECK ROUTE
PRACTICE RULE
Use eighth-note triplets: one three-note group per beat. Begin 15-20 BPM below your clean Level 23 tempo.
First master the 13 ascending triplets in A natural minor, then the 13 descending triplets. Link them
without restarting the pick cycle and make the two high-root notes equal in length and volume. Next use

Repeat with both pick starts. Remove the pause, connect the ladder, reverse after the fret-17 cell, and
return to fret 5. Add 2 BPM after three clean round trips. Reduce 4-6 BPM after two errors, a broken
triplet pulse, a missed backreach or B-string offset, dragged shift noise, or rising tension. Advance after
the complete route is clean with both pick starts on two separate days.

NATURAL MINOR FOUR-NOTE ROLLING SEQUENCE - ONE-OCTAVE NECK LADDER: A TO A
PURPOSE

40-note up/down rolling cell, release pressure, move the entire hand-and-thumb frame exactly one fret,

Level 24 expanded the three-note rolling sequence across two octaves and all six strings. Level 25
deliberately returns to the compact three-string octave so the new four-note overlap can be learned without
simultaneously managing the upper-octave backreach and B-string offset. Level 26 will extend this exact
sequence across the complete two-octave frame.
IMPORTANT INTERPRETATION
Moving one fixed scale shape by one fret transposes it. A natural minor is the starting rung, not the key of every rung.
A fixed-key A-natural-minor exercise in every neck position requires changing the note layout and remains a separate branch.
NATURAL-MINOR FORMULA

Intervals: whole - half - whole - whole - half - whole - whole

Low E string: R, R+2, R+3          Fingers 1,3,4
A string:     R, R+2, R+3          Fingers 1,3,4
D string:     R, R+2               Fingers 1,3
The four-fret hand frame runs from R through R+3.
Ascending notes per string: 3-3-2. Descending notes per string: 2-3-3.

Each new group begins one scale degree farther along. At every group boundary, the line drops a diatonic
third and then continues forward. Three notes overlap from one group to the next. Do not pause, accent,
or reset at a group boundary.

DOWN: DDAA | DAAA | AAAE | AAEE | AEEE
The crossings move from late to balanced to early as the line travels across the three-string frame.
Keep the first note after every crossing equal in volume and time.

The complete up/down cell contains 10 groups and 40 notes. The octave root is repeated at the turn:
the last note of 5-b6-b7-8 is followed by the first note of 8-b7-b6-5. Because 40 is even, the next
key begins with the same pick orientation. Because every group has four notes, every group also begins

D-start groups: D-U-D-U | D-U-D-U | D-U-D-U ... through all 10 groups.
U-start groups: U-D-U-D | U-D-U-D | U-D-U-D ... through all 10 groups.
Never restart the pick cycle at a new group, string crossing, scale turn, or one-fret shift.
NECK ROUTE
PRACTICE RULE
Use sixteenth notes: one four-note group per beat. Begin at roughly 75 percent of your clean Level 24
metronome setting; for example, if Level 24 is clean at 80 BPM, begin near 60 BPM. Master the A-natural-

guidance_lines.text: SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION III, LEVEL 27
NATURAL MINOR DIATONIC THIRDS - TWO-OCTAVE SIX-STRING NECK LADDER
PURPOSE
Level 27 leaves stepwise and rolling natural-minor motion and begins intervallic sequencing.
Each pair skips one scale degree: 1-b3, 2-4, b3-5, and onward. After each upper note,
the next pair rolls back one degree and continues upward. The exercise retains the same
two-octave six-string natural-minor shape and one-fret chromatic neck route used in Levels
WHAT CHANGES FROM LEVEL 26
Level 26 moved in overlapping four-note scale fragments. Level 27 replaces those fragments
with two-note diatonic thirds. The mechanical demand is shorter, but the musical demand is
higher: hear whether each pair is a minor third or major third, preserve the one-degree
rollback, and keep every string crossing inside one uninterrupted line.
NATURAL-MINOR FORMULA
One octave: 1 2 b3 4 5 b6 b7 8
Two octaves: 1 2 b3 4 5 b6 b7 8 9 b10 11 12 b13 b14 15
Intervals: whole - half - whole - whole - half - whole - whole, then repeat
MAIN SEQUENCE
Each new pair begins one scale position farther forward. Between pairs, the line rolls back
one degree: 1-b3 then 2-4; 4-b6 then 5-b7. Do not pause or reset at the rollback.
INTERVAL-QUALITY PATTERN
Ascending:  m3 | m3 | M3 | m3 | m3 | M3 | M3 | m3 | m3 | M3 | m3 | m3 | M3
Descending: M3 | m3 | m3 | M3 | m3 | m3 | M3 | M3 | m3 | m3 | M3 | m3 | m3
M3 = major third = 4 semitones. m3 = minor third = 3 semitones.
First-octave natural-minor pattern: m3 | m3 | M3 | m3 | m3 | M3 | M3.
Natural minor uses the same two third sizes as major, but the order begins differently.
TWO-OCTAVE SIX-STRING SHAPE - ROOT FRET R ON LOW E
Low E string: R, R+2, R+3          Fingers 1,3,4        Positions 1,2,b3
A string:     R, R+2, R+3          Fingers 1,3,4        Positions 4,5,b6
D string:     R, R+2               Fingers 1,3          Positions b7,8
G string:     R-1, R, R+2          Fingers 1,2,4        Positions 9,b10,11
B string:     R, R+1, R+3          Fingers 1,2,4        Positions 12,b13,b14
High e:       R                    Finger 1             Position 15
The complete map spans R-1 through R+3. Release and rebuild for the G-string backreach and
again for the B-string offset; do not hold a static five-fret stretch.
STRING-PATH MAP
Ascending:  EE | EA | EA | AA | AD | AD | DG | DG | GG | GB | GB | BB | Be
Descending: eB | BB | BG | BG | GG | GD | GD | DA | DA | AA | AE | AE | EE
Some thirds stay on one string; others cross one string boundary. Keep every landing equal
in volume and preserve the two-note pulse through the D-G and G-B transitions.
CELL DESIGN
- 13 ascending pairs / 26 notes
- repeat the high root at the turnaround
- 13 descending pairs / 26 notes
- 52 notes total per key
- shift the entire hand-and-thumb frame one fret only after the final b3-1 pair
PICKING
Downstroke start: D-U | D-U | D-U | ... through all 26 pairs.
Upstroke start:   U-D | U-D | U-D | ... through all 26 pairs.
Because each pair and the complete 52-note cell are even, every pair and every new key begins
with the same pick orientation. Do not reset at a string crossing, the middle octave, the
repeated high root, or a new key.
RHYTHM
Learning pulse: one pair per beat as eighth notes.
Performance pulse: two pairs per beat as straight sixteenth notes.
Accent the first note of each pair while learning, then remove the accents and equalize all notes.
PRACTICE PROGRESSION
1. A natural minor, first octave only: pairs 1-b3 through b6-8, then reverse.
2. A natural minor, all 13 ascending pairs.
3. A natural minor, all 13 descending pairs.
4. Link the 52-note cell; articulate both high-root notes without resetting.
5. Use two or three neighboring keys with a one-beat pause only after each complete cell.
6. Remove the pause and complete the entire route with both pick starts.
CHROMATIC ROUTE
Down: G# -> G -> F# -> F -> E -> Eb -> D -> C# -> C -> B -> Bb -> A
Do not replay the high A-natural-minor rung during the down pass unless beginning a new round.

SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION III, LEVEL 28
NATURAL MINOR DIATONIC TRIADS - TWO-OCTAVE SIX-STRING NECK LADDER
PURPOSE
Level 28 stacks one more scale tone onto the diatonic-thirds idea from Level 27. Every group now plays
a root, third, and fifth: 1-b3-5, 2-4-b6, b3-5-b7, and onward. The exercise converts natural
minor into a connected chain of broken triads while retaining the same two-octave six-string shape
and one-fret chromatic neck route.
WHAT CHANGES FROM LEVEL 27
Level 27 isolated two-note thirds and their major/minor qualities. Level 28 adds the diatonic fifth,
turning every interval pair into a complete triad. The mechanical demand becomes a three-note group
that may span one, two, or three strings; the musical demand is to hear and name i, ii diminished,
III, iv, v, VI, and VII without losing the continuous triplet pulse.
NATURAL-MINOR FORMULA
One octave: 1 2 b3 4 5 b6 b7 8
Two octaves: 1 2 b3 4 5 b6 b7 8 9 b10 11 12 b13 b14 15
Intervals: whole - half - whole - whole - half - whole - whole, then repeat
MAIN SEQUENCE
Each new triad begins one scale position farther forward. The line climbs a third and another third,
then rolls back three scale positions to begin the next chord. Do not pause or reset at the rollback.
HARMONIC FUNCTION AND QUALITY
Ascending:  i minor | ii diminished | III major | iv minor | v minor | VI major | VII major | i minor | ii diminished | III major | iv minor
Descending: iv minor | III major | ii diminished | i minor | VII major | VI major | v minor | iv minor | III major | ii diminished | i minor
Natural minor has a minor v and a major VII because degree b7 is not raised. Harmonic minor will alter
those functions later; do not import the raised seventh into this workbook.
TWO-OCTAVE SIX-STRING SHAPE - ROOT FRET R ON LOW E
Low E string: R, R+2, R+3          Fingers 1,3,4        Positions 1,2,b3
A string:     R, R+2, R+3          Fingers 1,3,4        Positions 4,5,b6
D string:     R, R+2               Fingers 1,3          Positions b7,8
G string:     R-1, R, R+2          Fingers 1,2,4        Positions 9,b10,11
B string:     R, R+1, R+3          Fingers 1,2,4        Positions 12,b13,b14
High e:       R                    Finger 1             Position 15
The complete map spans R-1 through R+3. Release and rebuild for the G-string backreach and again for
the B-string offset; do not hold a static five-fret stretch.
STRING-PATH MAP
Ascending:  EEA | EAA | EAD | AAD | ADG | ADG | DGG | DGB | GGB | GBB | GBe
Descending: eBG | BBG | BGG | BGD | GGD | GDA | GDA | DAA | DAE | AAE | AEE
Some triads remain on two strings, while others span three strings. Keep the middle note rhythmically
centered and every landing equal in volume through the D-G and G-B transitions.
CELL DESIGN
- 11 ascending triads / 33 notes
- repeat the high root at the turnaround as the first note of the descending line
- 11 descending triads / 33 notes
- 22 triads / 66 notes total per key
- shift the entire hand-and-thumb frame one fret only after the final 5-b3-1 triad
PICKING
Downstroke start: D-U-D | U-D-U | D-U-D | U-D-U ... through all 22 triads.
Upstroke start:   U-D-U | D-U-D | U-D-U | D-U-D ... through all 22 triads.
Every three-note triad flips the starting stroke of the next triad. The complete 66-note cell is even,
so every new key begins on the same pick orientation. Do not reset at group boundaries, string changes,
the middle octave, the repeated high root, or a new key.
RHYTHM
Learning pulse: one triad per beat as eighth-note triplets.
Performance pulse: two triads per beat as sixteenth-note triplets (sextuplets).
Accent the root of each triad while learning, then remove the accents and equalize every note.
PRACTICE PROGRESSION
1. A natural minor, first octave only: i through iv, then reverse.
2. A natural minor, all 11 ascending triads.
3. A natural minor, all 11 descending triads.
4. Link the 66-note cell; articulate both high-root notes without resetting.
5. Use two or three neighboring keys with a one-beat pause only after each complete cell.
6. Remove the pause and complete the entire route with both pick starts.
CHROMATIC ROUTE
Down: G# -> G -> F# -> F -> E -> Eb -> D -> C# -> C -> B -> Bb -> A
Do not replay the high A-natural-minor rung during the down pass unless beginning a new round.

SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION III, LEVEL 29
NATURAL MINOR SYNTHESIS CIRCUIT - TWO-OCTAVE SIX-STRING NECK LADDER
PURPOSE
Level 29 combines the established two-octave natural-minor movements from Levels 22, 24, 26, 27, and 28 into
one uninterrupted circuit. Complete all five modules in the same key before shifting the entire hand-and-thumb
frame one fret. Re-articulate the low root at every module boundary while preserving the alternate-picking cycle.
FIVE-MODULE CELL
A. Linear scale:          30 notes - low root to high root, repeat high root, return to low root
B. Three-note roll:       78 notes - 13 ascending triplets and 13 descending triplets
C. Four-note roll:        96 notes - 12 ascending groups and 12 descending groups
D. Diatonic thirds:       52 notes - 13 ascending pairs and 13 descending pairs
E. Diatonic triads:       66 notes - 11 ascending triads and 11 descending triads
TOTAL:                   322 notes per key
MODULE ORDER
Linear -> Three-note roll -> Four-note roll -> Diatonic thirds -> Diatonic triads -> shift one fret
NATURAL-MINOR FORMULA
One octave: 1 2 b3 4 5 b6 b7 8
Two octaves: 1 2 b3 4 5 b6 b7 8 9 b10 11 12 b13 b14 15
Intervals: whole - half - whole - whole - half - whole - whole, then repeat
PICKING
All five module counts are even. With a downstroke start, every module and every new key begins on a downstroke;
with an upstroke start, each begins on an upstroke. Do not reset at group boundaries, string changes, octave turns,
module boundaries, the G-string backreach, the B-string offset, or one-fret shifts.
RHYTHM
Learning mode: one note per metronome click through the complete circuit.
Native-pulse mode:
- Linear scale: 30 eighth notes = 15 beats
- Three-note roll: 78 eighth-note triplets = 26 beats
- Four-note roll: 96 sixteenth notes = 24 beats
- Diatonic thirds: 52 eighth notes = 26 beats
- Diatonic triads: 66 eighth-note triplets = 22 beats
TOTAL: 113 quarter-note beats per 322-note circuit
PRACTICE PROGRESSION
1. Learn each module separately in A natural minor.
2. Link adjacent module pairs: A-B, B-C, C-D, and D-E.
3. Play the complete A-natural-minor circuit with a short pause at every module boundary.
4. Remove the pauses while retaining a light accent on each new module root.
5. Remove the accents and use two or three neighboring keys.
6. Complete longer route sections with both a downstroke and an upstroke start.
CHROMATIC ROUTE
Down: G# -> G -> F# -> F -> E -> Eb -> D -> C# -> C -> B -> Bb -> A
Do not replay the high A-natural-minor rung during the down pass unless beginning a new round.
ROUTE COUNT
25 circuits x 322 notes = 8,050 picked notes.
25 circuits x 113 native-pulse beats = 2,825 quarter-note beats.
The full route is a capstone endurance test, not a required daily warm-up.

guidance_lines.text: SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION IV, LEVEL 30
MAJOR PENTATONIC ONE-OCTAVE ONE-FRET NECK LADDER: A TO A
PURPOSE
Learn one compact one-octave major-pentatonic shape, move the complete hand-and-thumb frame exactly one fret,
and repeat through every major-pentatonic key. Begin with A major pentatonic at low-E fret 5, climb to A major
pentatonic at fret 17, then reverse and return one fret at a time.
MAJOR SCALE VS MAJOR PENTATONIC
A major:             A B C# D E F# G# A
A major pentatonic:  A B C#   E F#    A
Degrees 4 and 7 are omitted. This removes the two half-step tensions 3-4 and 7-8 from the full major scale.
MAJOR-PENTATONIC FORMULA
Degrees:   1 2 3 5 6 8
Intervals: whole - whole - minor third - whole - minor third
COMPACT ONE-OCTAVE SHAPE - ROOT FRET R ON LOW E
Low E string: R, R+2               Fingers 2,4
A string:     R-1, R+2             Fingers 1,4
D string:     R-1, R+2             Fingers 1,4
The four-fret hand frame runs from R-1 through R+2.
Ascending notes per string: 2-2-2. Descending notes per string: 2-2-2.
CELL AND PICKING RULE
Play degrees 1-2-3-5-6-8, then 8-6-5-3-2-1. The octave root is repeated at the turn.
This creates 12 notes, so the next key begins with the same alternate-picking orientation.
D-start: D U D U D U | D U D U D U
U-start: U D U D U D | U D U D U D
Do not restart the pick cycle at the scale turn, a string crossing, or the one-fret shift.
IMPORTANT INTERPRETATION
Moving one fixed shape by one fret transposes it. A major pentatonic is the starting rung, not the key of every rung.
Holding A major pentatonic constant while connecting its five neck positions is a later branch of this section.
NECK ROUTE
PRACTICE RULE
First compare A major and A major pentatonic and identify the omitted 4th and 7th. Then use 3-4 neighboring
major-pentatonic rungs. Play even eighth notes and pause one beat after each 12-note cell. During the pause,
release pressure and move the complete frame one fret. Repeat with both pick starts. Then remove the pause,
connect the ladder, reverse at fret 17, and return to fret 5.
Add 2 BPM after three clean round trips. Reduce 4-6 BPM after two errors, dragged shift noise, or rising tension.
Advance after the complete route is clean with both pick starts on two separate days.

guidance_lines.text: SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION IV, LEVEL 31
MAJOR PENTATONIC TWO-OCTAVE SIX-STRING NECK LADDER: A TO A
PURPOSE
Extend the exact Level 30 major-pentatonic frame across all six strings and two full octaves. Play the complete
22-note up/down cell, release pressure, move the entire hand-and-thumb frame exactly one fret, and repeat through
every major-pentatonic key. Begin with A major pentatonic at low-E fret 5, climb to A major pentatonic at fret 17,
then reverse and return one fret at a time.
IMPORTANT INTERPRETATION
Moving one fixed shape by one fret transposes it. A major pentatonic is the starting rung, not the key of every rung.
Holding A major pentatonic constant while connecting its five positions is a later branch of Section IV.
MAJOR-PENTATONIC FORMULA
Degrees per octave: 1 2 3 5 6
Intervals: whole - whole - minor third - whole - minor third
The omitted degrees 4 and 7 remain absent in both octaves.
COMPACT TWO-OCTAVE SIX-STRING SHAPE - ROOT FRET R ON LOW E
Low E string: R, R+2               Fingers 2,4
A string:     R-1, R+2             Fingers 1,4
D string:     R-1, R+2             Fingers 1,4
G string:     R-1, R+1             Fingers 1,3
B string:     R, R+2               Fingers 2,4
High e string:R                    Finger 2
The four-fret hand frame runs from R-1 through R+2.
STRING-DISTRIBUTION RULE
Ascending note counts by string: 2 - 2 - 2 - 2 - 2 - 1.
Descending note counts by string: 1 - 2 - 2 - 2 - 2 - 2.
The G-to-B tuning offset changes the visible geometry. Rebuild the assigned fingering rather than copying the
G-string shape directly onto the B and high-e strings.
CELL AND PICKING RULE
Ascend from the low root through the middle root to the high root, repeat the high root at the turnaround,
then descend to the low root. The complete cell contains 22 notes, so the next key begins with the same
alternate-picking orientation.
D-start: strict D-U alternate picking through every crossing, root, turnaround, and one-fret relocation.
U-start: strict U-D alternate picking through every crossing, root, turnaround, and one-fret relocation.
Do not restart the pick cycle on a new string, at the middle root, at the high-root turn, or after shifting.
NECK ROUTE
PRACTICE RULE
Begin 10-15 BPM below your clean Level 30 tempo. First master the A-major-pentatonic cell alone. Then use 2-3
neighboring rungs, play even eighth notes, and pause one beat after each 22-note cell while moving the complete
frame one fret. Repeat with both pick starts. Remove the pause, connect the ladder, reverse at fret 17, and return
to fret 5. Add 2 BPM after three clean round trips. Reduce 4-6 BPM after two errors, crossing noise, dragged shifts,
or rising tension. Advance after the full route is clean with both pick starts on two separate days.
SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION IV, LEVEL 32
MAJOR PENTATONIC THREE-NOTE ROLL AND FIVE-NOTE CYCLE - TWO-OCTAVE SIX-STRING NECK LADDER: A TO A
PURPOSE
Keep the Level 31 two-octave major-pentatonic frame and reorganize its eleven ordered scale positions
into two overlapping odd-count sequence modules. Practice each module separately, then link both modules
before moving the complete hand-and-thumb frame exactly one fret. Begin with A major pentatonic at low-E
fret 5, climb to the octave A at fret 17, then reverse and return one fret at a time.
MAJOR-PENTATONIC FORMULA
Degrees per octave: 1 2 3 5 6 8
Intervals: whole - whole - minor third - whole - minor third
The complete two-octave position line is: 1 2 3 5 6 8 9 10 12 13 15.
TWO-OCTAVE SIX-STRING SHAPE - ROOT FRET R ON LOW E
Low E string: R, R+2               Fingers 2,4
A string:     R-1, R+2             Fingers 1,4
D string:     R-1, R+2             Fingers 1,4
G string:     R-1, R+1             Fingers 1,3
B string:     R, R+2               Fingers 2,4
High e string: R                   Finger 2
The four-fret frame runs from R-1 through R+2. Do not change the Level 31 fingering.
MODULE A - THREE-NOTE ROLL
Each new triplet begins one pentatonic position farther along. The module contains 18 triplets and 54 notes.
Native grouped pulse: one eighth-note triplet per beat.
String paths up:   EEA | EAA | AAD | ADD | DDG | DGG | GGB | GBB | BBe
String paths down: eBB | BBG | BGG | GGD | GDD | DDA | DAA | AAE | AEE
MODULE B - FIVE-NOTE CYCLE
Each group contains five consecutive pentatonic positions and restarts one position farther along.
The module contains 14 quintuplets and 70 notes. Native grouped pulse: one quintuplet per beat.
String paths up:   EEAAD | EAADD | AADDG | ADDGG | DDGGB | DGGBB | GGBBe
String paths down: eBBGG | BBGGD | BGGDD | GGDDA | GDDAA | DDAAE | DAAEE
PICKING AND CELL RULE
Every three-note or five-note group is odd, so the starting stroke reverses at the next group.
Module A D-start: D-U-D | U-D-U | D-U-D ...
Module B D-start: D-U-D-U-D | U-D-U-D-U | D-U-D-U-D ...
Use the mirrored patterns for an upstroke start. Module A has 54 notes and Module B has 70 notes; both
totals are even. Therefore Module B and every new key begin with the original pick orientation.
Do not reset the pick at a group, string crossing, middle root, high-root turn, module boundary, or shift.
RHYTHM MODES
Grouped mode: one triplet or one quintuplet per beat. Learn this version first.
Displacement mode: play continuous sixteenth notes and let the three- or five-note group accent migrate
across 4/4. Treat displacement as a variation only after the grouped pulse is secure.
NECK ROUTE
COUNTS
Module A: 54 notes / 18 beats per key; 25-cell round trip = 1,350 notes.
Module B: 70 notes / 14 beats per key; 25-cell round trip = 1,750 notes.
Linked A+B: 124 notes / 32 beats per key; 25-cell round trip = 3,100 notes / 800 beats.

SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION IV, LEVEL 33
MAJOR PENTATONIC INTERVAL PAIRS AND MELODIC SKIPS - TWO-OCTAVE SIX-STRING NECK LADDER: A TO A
PURPOSE
Keep the Level 31 two-octave major-pentatonic frame and reorganize its eleven ordered scale positions into
two interval-focused modules. Module A skips one pentatonic tone to create adjacent-string interval pairs.
Module B makes a wider leap, then resolves to the skipped upper tone. Practice each module separately, link
both modules, then move the complete hand-and-thumb frame exactly one fret. Begin with A major pentatonic
at low-E fret 5, climb to the octave A at fret 17, then reverse and return one fret at a time.
MAJOR-PENTATONIC FORMULA
Degrees per octave: 1 2 3 5 6
Intervals: whole - whole - minor third - whole - minor third
Two-octave ordered positions: 1 2 3 5 6 8 9 10 12 13 15.
TWO-OCTAVE SIX-STRING SHAPE - ROOT FRET R ON LOW E
Low E string:  R, R+2               Fingers 2,4                  Positions 1,2
A string:      R-1, R+2             Fingers 1,4                  Positions 3,5
D string:      R-1, R+2             Fingers 1,4                  Positions 6,8
G string:      R-1, R+1             Fingers 1,3                  Positions 9,10
B string:      R, R+2               Fingers 2,4                  Positions 12,13

MODULE A - SKIP-ONE INTERVAL PAIRS
INT:  M3  | P4  | P4  | P4  | P4  | M3   | P4   | P4    | P4
Each pair skips one pentatonic position and lands on the next physical string. The module contains 18 pairs
and 36 notes. Native pulse: one two-note pair per beat as eighth notes.

MODULE B - WIDE-LEAP RESOLVE
The first two notes leap across three ordered pentatonic positions; the third note resolves to the skipped
upper position. First-leap qualities are P5 or m6. Resolution qualities are M2 or m3. The module contains
16 triplets and 48 notes. Native pulse: one eighth-note triplet per beat.

semantic_guidance.seam_instruction_text:
For each string, play lower outer note -> shared anchor -> upper outer note -> shared anchor -> lower outer note.
Stay in the lower-position fingering through note 2. Shift after the anchor sounds, play note 3 in the upper
frame, return to the anchor as note 4, then shift back before note 5. Do not re-articulate the anchor merely
to disguise the hand movement.
semantic_guidance.forward_route_text:
Route: P1 ASC -> high-e 7 to 9 -> P2 DESC -> low-E 7 to 9 -> P3 ASC -> high-e 12 to 14 ->
       P4 DESC -> low-E 12 to 14 -> P5 ASC.
Every position segment contains 12 notes, so every new frame begins with the same pick orientation.
semantic_guidance.reverse_route_text:
Route: P5 DESC -> low-E 14 to 12 -> P4 ASC -> high-e 14 to 12 -> P3 DESC -> low-E 9 to 7 ->
       P2 ASC -> high-e 9 to 7 -> P1 DESC.
When linking forward and reverse, articulate high-e fret 17 at the end of the forward route and again to
begin the reverse route. The linked circuit contains 120 notes and returns to low-E fret 5.
semantic_guidance.practice_mastery_text:
PRACTICE PROGRESSION
========================================================================================================================
1. Map P1-P5 and say each starting degree.
2. Play every 24-note vertical cell with both pick starts.
3. Learn all four 30-note shared-anchor seam cells.
4. Play the 60-note forward zigzag without a seam pause.
5. Play the 60-note reverse zigzag without a seam pause.
6. Link forward and reverse as one 120-note circuit.
7. Accent every A root, then remove the accents while continuing to hear A as tonic.

ERROR DIAGNOSIS
LOST KEY CENTER: Stop on the nearest A root, sing A, and restart the local frame.
WRONG BOX: Name the position span and its first low-E degree before playing.
EARLY SHIFT: Remain in the lower frame through the shared anchor; move only after it sounds.
NOISY SEAM: Release pressure, move the thumb with the hand, and reduce the tempo by 4-6 BPM.
PICK RESET: Mute the strings and air-pick the exact 12-, 30-, or 60-note count.
TENSION: Stop, shake out, and practice one seam instead of forcing the full route.

ADVANCEMENT RULES
Add 2 BPM after three clean circuits at the current route length.
After two errors, reduce 4-6 BPM or shorten the route to one adjacent-position seam.
Increase route length before speed when the shift is weak. Increase speed before route length when the map is secure.

MASTERY GATE BEFORE LEVEL 35
Name all five positions and fret spans; play each vertical cell with D-start and U-start; shift at every
shared anchor without a scrape or hesitation; complete the linked 120-note zigzag on two separate days;
identify every A root by sight and sound; and recover the correct position after a deliberate random stop.

guidance_lines.text: SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION IV, LEVEL 36
A MAJOR PENTATONIC EXPRESSIVE ARTICULATION - LEGATO, SLIDES, BENDS, RELEASES, AND VIBRATO
FIXED KEY A - FIVE POSITIONS - FRETS 4-17
PURPOSE
Turn the fixed-key A-major-pentatonic map from Levels 34-35 into controlled expressive motion. The pitch map
does not change. What changes is how each pitch begins, connects, bends, releases, and sustains. Train hammer-ons
and pull-offs in all five positions, combine legato with the four shared-anchor seams, calibrate whole-step bends
against named target frets, add pre-bend releases and pitch-centered vibrato, then finish with five short cadences.
IMPORTANT INTERPRETATION
Expression does not excuse inaccurate rhythm or pitch. A hammer-on, pull-off, slide arrival, bend target, release,
or vibrato pulse is a timed musical event. Picked and unpicked notes must remain equal in volume and duration.
All core bends in this level are whole-step bends to a note two frets higher. The minor-third gaps 3->5 and 6->1
would require a one-and-a-half-step bend and are deliberately excluded from the core bend module.
A MAJOR PENTATONIC
Notes: A B C# E F#
Degrees: 1 2 3 5 6
ARTICULATION NOTATION
h = hammer-on; p = pull-off; / = ascending slide; \ = descending slide; b(T) = bend to target fret T;
r = release; pb(T) = pre-bend silently to target pitch before the attack; ~ = vibrato.
COUNTS
Module A: 5 position cells x 24 sounding tones = 120 tones; 12 attacks per cell = 60 attacks.
Module B: 4 seams x 6 strings x 5 tones = 120 tones; one attack per phrase = 24 attacks.
Module C: 9 whole-step bend sites x 4 attacks = 36 attacks.
Module D: 6 pre-bend cells x 3 attacks = 18 attacks; 8 A-root vibrato holds = 8 attacks.
Module E: 5 cadence phrases = 19 attacks; articulation creates the remaining pitch motion.
Complete core workout: 165 pick attacks, plus 240 explicitly counted legato/slide tones, 15 bend or pre-bend
cells, 8 root-vibrato holds, and 5 cadence phrases.
MODULE A - FIVE-POSITION LEGATO CELLS
Pick the first tone of each two-note group. Hammer the ascending partner and pull off the descending partner.
Each position contains 12 groups, 24 sounding tones, and 12 pick attacks. Alternate the group attacks continuously.
D-start groups: D U D U D U | D U D U D U. U-start groups: U D U D U D | U D U D U D.

txt_lines_140_147: MODULE B - ONE-PICK FIVE-TONE SEAM CHAINS
Phrase rule: lower note h shared anchor / upper note \ shared anchor p lower note. Pick only the first tone.
Do not hold a rigid wide stretch at the outer destination. Release the lower finger during the outward slide and
replant it during the return so the final pull-off is prepared. First use one tone per click; later use quintuplets.
txt_lines_183_190: Core cell: play the target fret; play the source and bend to the target; play the source and bend-release;
finish by re-playing the target with narrow vibrato. Four attacks per site. Bend toward the center of the neck.
Use the ring finger supported by the index and middle fingers where practical. Mute adjacent strings.

controlled release. The final bend reaches the same target and adds narrow vibrato only after the pitch is stable.
txt_lines_223_228: Vibrato passes: 4 pulses per whole note; 6 pulses per whole note; then free vibrato while returning to the
original pitch between pulses. On a bent note, reach the target first and vibrate around that target.
MODULE E - FIVE POSITION EXPRESSIVE CADENCES

bend arrival, release, or held vibrato note.
PRACTICE PROGRESSION
1. Map the notation and say the A-major-pentatonic notes and degrees before playing.
2. Complete one Position 1 legato cell at one sounding tone per click.
3. Play all five Module A cells with both D-start and U-start attack cycles.
4. Add one seam page; keep all five tones equal from a single attack.
5. Calibrate one bend site by alternating the fretted target and bent target.
6. Complete all nine bend cells without overshooting, sagging, or adjacent-string noise.
7. Add pre-bend releases, then the eight A-root vibrato holds.
8. Play the five cadences separately, then link them without extra attacks.
ERROR DIAGNOSIS
WEAK HAMMER: strike closer to the fret with less travel; do not squeeze harder with the thumb.
EMPTY PULL-OFF: keep the destination fretted and use a tiny lateral pluck rather than simply lifting.
LATE SLIDE: shorten the motion; the arrival fret is a counted tone, not transportation.
FLAT BEND: support the bending finger, rotate the wrist, and compare directly with the target fret.
SHARP BEND: stop pushing after the target; hold the pitch before adding vibrato.
WIDE VIBRATO: reduce the motion until every pulse returns to the pitch center.
STRING NOISE: mute above the bend with the fretting index and below it with the picking hand.
PAIN OR TENSION: stop. Do not force the whole-step bend or substitute a one-and-a-half-step bend.

Add 2 BPM after three clean runs at the current module length. After two errors, reduce 4-6 BPM or isolate one
string, seam, bend, or cadence. Intonation outranks speed. Use a clean tone until the pitch and muting are stable.

scoop; hold all eight A roots with controlled vibrato; link the five cadence phrases on two separate days; and
identify the note and degree of every bend source, bend target, and final root.

A MAJOR PENTATONIC I-IV-V CHORD-TONE TARGETING AND VOICE LEADING
FIXED KEY A - FIVE POSITIONS - A, D, AND E MAJOR HARMONY
PURPOSE
Turn the fixed-key A-major-pentatonic map into harmony-aware phrasing. Keep the same five notes and five positions,
but stop treating every note as equally stable. Hear the active I, IV, or V chord; land on a strong chord tone at
the change; use the remaining pentatonic notes as motion; then resolve before the harmony changes again.
A MAJOR PENTATONIC
Notes: A B C# E F#
Degrees: 1 2 3 5 6
I-IV-V chords: A major = A C# E; D major = D F# A; E major = E G# B.
CORE TARGETS AVAILABLE INSIDE A MAJOR PENTATONIC
I - A major: A root, C# third, E fifth.
IV - D major: F# third, A fifth. The D root is not in A major pentatonic.
V - E major: E root, B fifth. The G# third is not in A major pentatonic.
Module D adds D and G# temporarily as chord-completion tones; they are not new pentatonic degrees.
CHORD-ROLE MATRIX
Note | Over A | Over D | Over E
A over E functions as 11/sus4 tension. C# over D functions as major-7 tension. Use either as motion, not an
unresolved downbeat landing, until the ear clearly hears the intended color.

Complete written workout: 496 sounding tones before optional articulation overlays.

PRACTICE PROGRESSION
1. Speak the I-IV-V chord tones and the five-note role matrix.
2. Complete one Position-1 target cell for each chord with both pick starts.
3. Play all fifteen target cells; hear the active chord before each cell.
4. Hold the three voice-leading routes as whole notes in all five positions.
5. Play one four-bar phrase and verify every beat-1 landing.
6. Add all five phrases, then one Level-36 articulation per bar.
7. Add D* and G#* through the five completion cadences.
8. Complete the 12-bar model chorus, then create a new fill while preserving its targets.

ERROR DIAGNOSIS
SCALE-RUN AUTOPILOT: stop the fill; play only one whole-note target per chord.
WEAK CHORD CHANGE: sing the next target before the bar arrives; reduce the fill to two notes.
D-CHORD C# LANDING: treat C# as major-7 tension and resolve immediately to D*, B, or a printed strong target.
E-CHORD A LANDING: treat A as suspended 11 tension and resolve to G#*, B, or E.
FRET SEARCH: name the string and fret before leaving the current target.
OVERFILLED BAR: leave beat 4 empty; silence is part of the phrase.
PICK OR ARTICULATION RESET: preserve the target rhythm first; expression is secondary.

MASTERY GATE BEFORE LEVEL 38
Identify the role of every A-major-pentatonic note over A, D, and E; play all fifteen target cells with both pick
starts; perform all three voice-leading routes in all five positions; land every written phrase target on beat 1;
use D and G# only over their supporting chords; complete the 12-bar chorus on two separate days; and improvise one
new chorus whose chord changes remain audible without a backing track.

NEXT LEVEL
Level 38 combines the five positions, horizontal movement, articulation, and I-IV-V targeting into call-and-response
phrasing and controlled improvisation synthesis.

guidance_lines.text: SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION IV, LEVEL 38
A MAJOR PENTATONIC CALL-AND-RESPONSE PHRASING AND IMPROVISATION SYNTHESIS
FIXED KEY A - FIVE POSITIONS - HARMONY A, D, AND E MAJOR
PURPOSE
Combine the five fixed-key positions, horizontal movement, expressive articulation, and I-IV-V chord targets
into phrases that sound intentional rather than like scale recitation. Build a short call, leave measured space,
answer the active harmony, develop one recognizable motif, and preserve the chord change while moving across the neck.
A MAJOR PENTATONIC
Notes: A B C# E F#
Degrees: 1 2 3 5 6
I-IV-V chords: A major = A C# E; D major = D F# A; E major = E G# B.
Strong pentatonic targets: A/C#/E over A; F#/A over D; E/B over E.
Completion tones: D* may appear only over D major; G#* may appear only over E major.
PHRASE GRAMMAR
A call states a rhythm and contour, then leaves room. It often ends on degree 2 or 6 rather than a final tonic.
A response may echo the rhythm, reverse the contour, move to a neighboring position, or change the chord target.
Silence is counted. A rest is not lost time; it is part of the phrase. A response should arrive because the harmony
changed, not because the player ran out of scale notes.
TAB LEGEND
P = picked attack; h = hammer-on destination; p = pull-off destination; s = slide destination;
b = bend destination; r = rest; = = held tone. Continue alternate picking only through actual picked attacks.
The count row shows eighth-note slots: 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 &.
CORE WRITTEN COUNTS
Module A local question/answer pairs: 55 sounding tones / 37 pick attacks.
Module B four seam phrases: 97 sounding tones / 62 pick attacks.
Module C motif transformation lab: 30 sounding tones / 23 pick attacks.
Module D space and density ladder: 60 sounding tones / 60 pick attacks.
Module E model 12-bar chorus: 70 sounding tones / 55 pick attacks.
Complete written workout: 312 sounding tones / 237 pick attacks, before the controlled free choruses.
MODULE A - FIVE LOCAL QUESTION-AND-ANSWER PAIRS
Each call and response uses one position and two bars of eighth-note slots. The call leaves an open color;
the response preserves enough of the rhythm to sound related and ends on an A-major chord tone. Practice the call,
count one full bar of silence, play the response, then remove the extra bar while keeping the phrase boundary audible.

PURPOSE
Introduce the genuinely new A minor pentatonic pitch set, keep A as the fixed tonic, and connect five common
positions across the neck. Learn each vertical frame, shift only after the shared anchor at every adjacent-position
seam, then link all five boxes in forward and reverse zigzags.
IMPORTANT PARALLEL-MINOR DISTINCTION
A major pentatonic:  A B C# E F#   degrees 1 2 3 5 6
F# minor pentatonic: F# A B C# E   same notes as A major, re-centered in Levels 39-40
A minor pentatonic:  A C D E G     degrees 1 b3 4 5 b7
A minor pentatonic is the parallel-minor pitch collection. It is not the same fret map with renamed degrees.
A MINOR-PENTATONIC FORMULA
Notes: A C D E G
Degrees: 1 b3 4 5 b7
Intervals: minor third - whole - whole - minor third - whole
POSITION-LABEL NOTE
Pentatonic box numbers vary among methods. This workbook numbers positions in ascending-neck order beginning
with the standard A-minor root frame at fret 5. Fret spans, degree maps, and root locations are authoritative.

Ascending degrees: 1 b3 4 5 b7 1 b3 4 5 b7 1 b3

Ascending degrees: b3 4 5 b7 1 b3 4 5 b7 1 b3 4

Ascending degrees: 4 5 b7 1 b3 4 5 b7 1 b3 4 5

P5 FLAT-SEVENTH FRAME       frets 14-17 starts b7 roots E17, G14, e17

PICKING AND COUNTS
Each vertical position cell contains 24 notes: 12 ascending and 12 descending with the highest endpoint repeated.

PURPOSE
Introduce the genuinely new A minor pentatonic pitch set, keep A as the fixed tonic, and connect five common
positions across the neck. Learn each vertical frame, shift only after the shared anchor at every adjacent-position
seam, then link all five boxes in forward and reverse zigzags.

IMPORTANT PARALLEL-MINOR DISTINCTION
A major pentatonic:  A B C# E F#   degrees 1 2 3 5 6
F# minor pentatonic: F# A B C# E   same notes as A major, re-centered in Levels 39-40
A minor pentatonic:  A C D E G     degrees 1 b3 4 5 b7
A minor pentatonic is the parallel-minor pitch collection. It is not the same fret map with renamed degrees.

A MINOR-PENTATONIC FORMULA
Notes: A C D E G
Degrees: 1 b3 4 5 b7
Intervals: minor third - whole - whole - minor third - whole

POSITION-LABEL NOTE
Pentatonic box numbers vary among methods. This workbook numbers positions in ascending-neck order beginning
with the standard A-minor root frame at fret 5. Fret spans, degree maps, and root locations are authoritative.

POSITION SUMMARY
P1 ROOT FRAME               frets 5-8   starts 1  roots E5, D7, e5
    Ascending degrees: 1 b3 4 5 b7 1 b3 4 5 b7 1 b3
P2 FLAT-THIRD FRAME         frets 7-10  starts b3 roots D7, B10
    Ascending degrees: b3 4 5 b7 1 b3 4 5 b7 1 b3 4
P3 FOURTH-DEGREE FRAME      frets 9-13  starts 4  roots A12, B10
    Ascending degrees: 4 5 b7 1 b3 4 5 b7 1 b3 4 5
P4 FIFTH-DEGREE FRAME       frets 12-15 starts 5  roots A12, G14
    Ascending degrees: 5 b7 1 b3 4 5 b7 1 b3 4 5 b7
P5 FLAT-SEVENTH FRAME       frets 14-17 starts b7 roots E17, G14, e17
    Ascending degrees: b7 1 b3 4 5 b7 1 b3 4 5 b7 1

PICKING AND COUNTS
Each vertical position cell contains 24 notes: 12 ascending and 12 descending with the highest endpoint repeated.
Each shared-anchor seam cell contains 30 notes: six five-note string groups.
The forward zigzag contains 60 notes; the reverse zigzag contains 60 notes; linked circuit = 120 notes.
Five position cells = 120 notes. Four seam cells = 120 notes. Linked zigzag = 120 notes.
Complete Level 41 core map = 360 notes. Five parallel major/minor comparisons add 60 tones. Complete written workout = 420 tones.

STRICT ALTERNATE PICKING
Complete separate D-start and U-start passes. Do not restart at a string crossing, shared anchor, position
boundary, root, outer-string turn, or the forward/reverse turnaround.

========================================================================================================================
FIVE VERTICAL POSITION CELLS
========================================================================================================================
additional_verified_guidance.seam_rule_text:
For each string, play lower outer note -> shared anchor -> upper outer note -> shared anchor -> lower outer note.
Stay in the lower-position fingering through note 2. Shift after the anchor sounds, play note 3 in the upper
frame, return to the anchor as note 4, then shift back before note 5.
additional_verified_guidance.practice_mastery_text:
PRACTICE PROGRESSION
========================================================================================================================
1. Compare the A-major and A-minor pitch sets.
2. Map P1 and say 1-b3-4-5-b7 aloud.
3. Learn all five 24-note vertical cells.
4. Play every cell with D-start and U-start.
5. Learn all four 30-note shared-anchor seams.
6. Link the 60-note forward and reverse zigzags.
7. Accent every A root, then remove the accents.
8. Complete all five parallel-color comparisons.
9. Complete all ten random-position entry cards.

AFTER THE BASIC MAP IS CLEAN
1. Play one A-major-pentatonic position from Level 34, then answer in the corresponding A-minor position.
2. Begin at a randomly selected box, name its first degree, and resolve to the nearest A root.
3. Play root-to-root phrases that cross exactly one seam, then two seams, then all four.
4. Start from P5 and descend first.

ERROR DIAGNOSIS
LOST TONIC: Stop on the nearest A root, sing A, and restart the local frame.
WRONG BOX: Name the position span and starting degree before playing.
MAJOR/MINOR CONFUSION: Say A-C-D-E-G and compare it directly with A-B-C#-E-F#.
EARLY SHIFT: Remain in the lower frame through the shared anchor; move only after it sounds.
NOISY SEAM: Release pressure, move the thumb with the hand, and reduce the tempo by 4-6 BPM.
PICK RESET: Mute the strings and air-pick the exact 12-, 30-, 60-, or 120-note count.
TENSION: Stop, shake out, and practice one seam instead of forcing the complete route.

ADVANCEMENT RULES
Add 2 BPM after three clean circuits at the current route length.
After two errors, reduce 4-6 BPM or shorten the route to one adjacent-position seam.
Increase route length before speed when the map or seam is weak.

MASTERY GATE BEFORE LEVEL 42
Name all five positions and fret spans; distinguish A minor pentatonic from A major pentatonic by sound and
note name; play each vertical cell with D-start and U-start; shift at every shared anchor without scrape or
hesitation; complete the linked 120-note zigzag on two separate days; identify every A root by sight and sound;
resolve all ten random-entry cards to the assigned roots; identify all five major/minor color pairs by ear; and
recover the correct position after a deliberate random stop.

LINKED CADENCE CIRCUIT
Play P1 through P5 with one bar of rest between phrases. Then reduce the rest to two beats, one beat, and no
extra pause. Preserve the attack count; do not pick hammer, pull, slide, bend arrival, release, or vibrato pulses.

additional_verified_guidance.txt_practice_and_mastery:
PRACTICE PROGRESSION, ERROR REPAIR, AND MASTERY
========================================================================================================================
1. Say the six lane notes and degrees before playing.
2. Learn one Module A lane at one sounding tone per click.
3. Complete all six silent-shift cells with D-start and U-start.
4. Add Module B destination landings; remove fret fishing before increasing speed.
5. Practice one Module C seam, then convert it into the one-pick Module E chain.
6. Complete all five Module D legato cells with equal picked and unpicked volume.
7. Calibrate one whole-step bend against its printed target; then add the release.
8. Establish C# as the blue-third ceiling, then produce a deliberate shade below it.
9. Hold all eight A roots with centered vibrato.
10. Link the five cadence phrases without extra attacks or loss of tonic.

ERROR DIAGNOSIS
NOISY SHIFT: release earlier, move thumb with hand, reduce 4-6 BPM.
FRET FISHING: look at and name the destination before leaving the launch note.
WEAK HAMMER: strike closer to the fret with less travel; do not clamp the thumb.
EMPTY PULL-OFF: keep the destination fretted and use a tiny lateral pluck.
LATE SLIDE: shorten the motion; the destination is a counted tone.
FLAT OR SHARP BEND: compare directly with the fretted target and hold before releasing.
BLUE SHADE REACHES C#: reduce the motion; the full half-step is only the upper boundary.
WIDE VIBRATO: narrow the movement until every pulse returns to center.
STRING NOISE: mute above the bend with the index and below it with the picking hand.
PAIN OR TENSION: stop. Do not force a bend or hold a rigid five-fret stretch.

ADVANCEMENT
Add 2 BPM after three clean runs at the current module length. After two errors, reduce 4-6 BPM or isolate one
lane, seam, bend site, or cadence. Intonation and timing outrank speed. Use clean tone until muting is stable.

the five cadences on two separate days.

guidance_lines.text: SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION V, LEVEL 43
A BLUES SCALE MAP AND BLUE-NOTE CONTROL - FIXED KEY A
PURPOSE
Add Eb, the b5 blue note, to the complete A-minor-pentatonic map from Levels 41-42. Learn every
practical Eb location, insert it into all five positions, and control whether it passes quickly, resolves
to degree 4 or 5, slides chromatically, or remains exposed as deliberate tension.
A BLUES FORMULA
Notes:    A C D Eb E G
Degrees:  1 b3 4 b5 5 b7
Intervals: minor third - whole - half - half - minor third - whole
A minor pentatonic remains the five-note skeleton. Eb is the added b5; it is not a replacement for D or E.
BLUE-NOTE PRINCIPLE
The b5 is a controlled tension, not an automatically forbidden note and not an automatically stable one.
It may pass between 4 and 5, slide chromatically, or be sustained deliberately. The exercise fails only
when the duration or resolution is accidental.
NOTATION
h = hammer-on | / = slide upward | \ = slide downward | ~~~~ = sustain or vibrato | R = measured rest
CORE BLUE-NOTE ATLAS - D(4) -> Eb(b5) -> E(5)
P5 also uses the A-string octave extension A|17-18-19| = D-Eb-E.
CORE COUNTS
Module A: one- and two-octave reference cells = 40 tones / 40 attacks
Module B: five position insertion cells = 144 tones / 144 attacks
Module C: six chromatic resolution cells = 36 tones / 36 attacks
Module D: five four-note resolution pairs = 40 tones / 40 attacks
Module E: passing-versus-resting comparisons = 48 tones / 48 attacks
Module F: six chromatic slide chains = 36 tones / 12 attacks
Module G: four position-seam phrases = 24 tones / 8 attacks
Module H: three rhythmic-displacement studies = 18 tones / 18 attacks
Module I: six resolution-audit cards = 36 tones / 36 attacks
Complete written workout = 422 sounding tones / 382 pick attacks

Error diagnosis
- MISSING b5 - say 4-b5-5 before playing.
- D# SPELLING - use Eb in the A-blues context.

- ACCIDENTAL HOLD - choose passing or resting first.

- PICK RESET - air-pick the full cell count.

guidance_lines.text: SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION V, LEVEL 46
A7-D7-E7 CHORD-TONE TARGETING AND GUIDE-TONE VOICE LEADING - FIXED KEY A
PURPOSE
Make the twelve-bar A blues harmony audible through intentional chord-tone landings. Keep the A-blues vocabulary
available for motion, but treat the root, third, fifth, and flat seventh of the active dominant chord as structural
targets. Track the third and flat seventh as guide tones through the A7-D7-E7 form.
DOMINANT CHORD TONES
A7 = A C# E G      roles R 3 5 b7
D7 = D F# A C      roles R 3 5 b7
E7 = E G# B D      roles R 3 5 b7
GUIDE-TONE SHELLS
A7: C# + G    D7: F# + C    E7: G# + D
A7 -> D7: C#->C and G->F#.
D7 -> A7: C->C# and F#->G.
A7 -> E7: C#->D and G->G#.
E7 -> A7: D->C# and G#->G.
WRITTEN COUNTS
Module A target cells: 294 tones.
Module B guide-tone shells: 30 tones.
Module C beat-one target choruses: 48 tones.
Module D guide-tone lines: 120 tones.
Module E five position phrases: 80 tones.
Module F dominant-third arrivals: 60 tones.
Module G written twelve-bar chorus: 48 tones.
Module H recovery cards: 24 tones.
Complete written workload: 704 sounding tones before repeats.

Note | Over A7 | Over D7 | Over E7
A    | R          | 5          | 11           | tonic over A7; common tone into D7
C    | b3 / blue  | b7         | b13          | strong over D7; shade toward C# over A7
D    | 11         | R          | b7           | root of D7; guide tone over E7
Eb   | b5         | b9         | M7 chromatic | passing tension; do not land accidentally
E    | 5          | 9          | R            | stable over A7 and E7

Completion tones:

guidance_lines.text: SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION V, LEVEL 47
A MAJOR AND A MINOR PENTATONIC MIXING - CHORD-AWARE COLOR CONTROL - FIXED KEY A
PURPOSE
Combine A major pentatonic and A minor pentatonic intentionally without treating their union as a default
eight-note scale. Use A and E as common anchors, control the three color pairs, target the active dominant
chord, preserve the twelve-bar form, and explain every color change after playing it.
PITCH POOLS
A major pentatonic: A B C# E F#    degrees 1 2 3 5 6
A minor pentatonic: A C D E G      degrees 1 b3 4 5 b7
Common tones: A E

COLOR KEY
C = common to both sets; M = major-only; m = minor-only; * = chord-completion tone.
CORE MIXING GRAMMAR
ANCHOR -> COLOR -> CHORD TARGET -> SPACE
Do not run A-B-C-C#-D-E-F#-G as the default exercise. Keep one motif or anchor stable and change one
color decision at a time.

SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION V, LEVEL 47
A MAJOR AND A MINOR PENTATONIC MIXING - CHORD-AWARE COLOR CONTROL - FIXED KEY A

PURPOSE
Combine A major pentatonic and A minor pentatonic intentionally without treating their union as a default
eight-note scale. Use A and E as common anchors, control the three color pairs, target the active dominant
chord, preserve the twelve-bar form, and explain every color change after playing it.

PITCH POOLS
A major pentatonic: A B C# E F#    degrees 1 2 3 5 6
A minor pentatonic: A C D E G      degrees 1 b3 4 5 b7
Common tones: A E
Color pairs: C#/C, F#/G, B/D
E7 completion tone: G#* - not a pentatonic member.

COLOR KEY
C = common to both sets; M = major-only; m = minor-only; * = chord-completion tone.

CORE MIXING GRAMMAR
ANCHOR -> COLOR -> CHORD TARGET -> SPACE
Do not run A-B-C-C#-D-E-F#-G as the default exercise. Keep one motif or anchor stable and change one
color decision at a time.
