source_guidance.practice_mastery_text:
PRACTICE PROGRESSION
1. Name both pitch pools and all three color pairs.
2. Play one position foundation page against an A drone.
3. Complete all C/C# third-control sites.
4. Play the six two-bar switch studies.
5. Complete the four overlap seams.
6. Play all A7, D7, and E7 hybrid target cells.
7. Complete major-question/minor-answer and minor-question/major-answer in all five positions.
8. Play the minor-only and major-only choruses on separate days.
9. Play the mixed chorus and model chorus with beat-one targets intact.
10. Improvise three choruses: minor only, major only, then controlled mixture.

ERROR DIAGNOSIS
CHROMATIC SOUP: return to A or E and select one color pair only.
WEAK BARLINE: hold the next chord tone for a whole note.
C/C# BLUR: play both fretted targets before bending or sliding.
G# OVERUSE: restrict G# to E7 or a direct E7 approach.
MOTIF LOST: keep the rhythm and change only the final two notes.
FORM LOST: play one root-only chorus and count every bar aloud.

MASTERY GATE
- Name every color note and its set membership.
- Match C# at all six third-control sites.
- Complete all switch studies and overlap seams.
- Make A7, D7, and E7 audible through hybrid target cells.
- Perform minor-only, major-only, and mixed twelve-bar choruses without losing form.
- Record one mixed chorus and explain every major/minor color decision afterward.

NEXT LEVEL
Level 48 combines form, chord targeting, major/minor color, blues vocabulary, motif development, space,
and call-and-response into a three-chorus improvisation synthesis.

guidance_lines.text: SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION V, LEVEL 48
A BLUES CALL-AND-RESPONSE AND IMPROVISATION SYNTHESIS - FIXED KEY A
TWELVE-BAR FORM - FIVE POSITIONS - THREE-CHORUS CAPSTONE
PURPOSE
Combine the A-minor-pentatonic map, the flat-five blue note, shuffle rhythm, A7-D7-E7 chord targets,
major/minor color control, articulation, position movement, motif development, and deliberate space into
complete musical conversations. The objective is not to play more notes. The objective is to make the form,
the active chord, the motif, the phrase boundary, and the dynamic direction audible without losing the pulse.
PITCH POOLS
A minor pentatonic: A C D E G          degrees 1 b3 4 5 b7
A blues scale:        A C D Eb E G       adds b5
A major pentatonic:   A B C# E F#       degrees 1 2 3 5 6
Completion tone:      G# may appear as the third of E7. F may appear only as a marked chromatic approach.
TWELVE-BAR FORM
PHRASE GRAMMAR
A call states a rhythm, contour, register, color, or articulation and leaves a question. A response preserves
at least one recognizable feature while changing the chord target, contour, register, density, or ending.
Silence is counted. A position shift must sound like part of the sentence. The strongest target should arrive
because the harmony changed, not because the phrase ran out of notes.
TAB LEGEND
P = picked attack; h = hammer-on; p = pull-off; s = slide arrival; b = bend; b< = blue-third shade;
r = rest; = = held tone. Color row: C common anchor, m minor-only, b5 blue note, M major-only, * completion.

F triplet on beat 1, rest beat 2, quarter beats 3-4
G one attack then 3-beat sustain
H half-bar silence then 3-note pickup
Apply the same rhythm to three different pitch contours. The rhythm should remain recognizable.

Module B - Motif Transformation
Transformation Keep Change
Transposition interval/rhythm identity starting pitch
Sequence contour scale-degree level
Rhythmic augmentation pitch order durations longer
Rhythmic diminution pitch order durations shorter
Inversion rhythmic identity up/down contour
Retrograde rhythm or pitch set order
Register shift pitch classes/rhythm octave
Truncation opening identity remove ending
After each transformation, play original then variant. If the relationship is no longer audible, restore one identity feature.

Module B - Development Ladder
Bars Instruction
1-2 state motif exactly
3-4 transpose or sequence
5-6 change rhythm but retain contour
7 truncate motif
8 restore original or cadence version
Write four different eight-bar developments from one three- or four-note motif.

Module C - Harmony-First Constraints
Constraint Eight-bar assignment
Only I-IV-V create contrast without new chords
No V-I cadence find alternate arrival
One common tone in every chord voice-leading drives progression
Chromatic mediant once make it sound intentional
Descending bass only harmony follows bass direction
Pedal tone for 4 bars harmony changes above fixed note
One secondary dominant prepare one destination
Two chords only rhythm/register create form
Write the functional progression first, then voicings, then melody.

Module C - Harmonic Direction Audit
Question Pass condition
Where is tonic? listener can identify home
Where is strongest departure? one section/bar feels least settled
Where is cadence? arrival is audible
What voice leads most clearly? name bass/guide/common tone
Which chord is optional? remove it and compare
Does bar 8 close or turn around? intentional answer
A progression is not finished merely because eight chord symbols have been written.

Module D - Melody-First Writing
Pass Task
1 sing 4-8 bar melody with no guitar
2 write contour and rhythm
3 identify strong-beat notes
4 choose chords supporting those notes
5 test alternate bass under same melody
6 reduce harmony to bass + melody
7 add inner voices only if useful
Do not change the melody merely because the first chord grip is inconvenient.

Module D - One Melody, Four Harmonizations
Version Constraint
1 diatonic only
2 one secondary dominant
3 one borrowed/chromatic chord
4 bass line determines reharmonization
5 sparse: maximum two chords per four bars
6 dense: one chord per bar
Rank versions by melody support, bass direction, cadence strength, and distinctiveness.

Module E - Bass-First Composition
Bass design Assignment
Stepwise descent write harmony above C-B-A-G-F-E-D-G
Stepwise ascent A-B-C-D-E-F-G-A
Pedal A held/repeated for four bars
Root/fifth alternation country/Americana engine
Chromatic approach destination roots on beats 1
Syncopated riff harmony implied by bass rhythm
Contrary to melody bass down while melody rises
Sparse roots melody supplies harmonic color
Sing a possible top line while playing bass before adding chords.

Module E - Bass/Harmony Independence
Pass Bass Harmony
1 fixed roots only
2 fixed triads
3 fixed 7th chords
4 fixed alternate inversions
5 simplified retain harmonic function
6 new bass retain top melody
The bass line is compositional material, not merely the bottom note of a chord grip.

Module F - Rhythm-First Composition
Groove engine Constraint
Funk one 2-beat syncopated cell for 8 bars
Rock one pedal/accent riff, three variations
Reggae offbeat pattern; harmony changes without changing rhythm
Shuffle triplet spacing; motif enters every 2 bars
Soul backbeat shell + one answer window
Country alternating bass/chord engine
Interlock upper repeated cell around bass space
Jam-band one motif, density changes only
Write rhythm first on muted strings. Add harmony only after the groove has identity.

Module F - Same Harmony, Four Rhythmic Identities
Use | Am7 | Fmaj7 | Cmaj7 | G7 | x2.
Version Rhythmic identity

The chord progression stays unchanged. The composition should feel substantially different because rhythm is structural.

Module G - Eight-Bar Constraint Laboratory
Card Required constraints

2 descending bass; melody rises; no V-I

5 melody-first; one common tone across all harmony
6 bass-first; one secondary dominant; sparse melody

8 one articulation family only; dynamics create climax
Complete all eight cards. Do not revise while generating the first draft; revise only after a full eight bars exist.

Module H - Study 1 - Motif first
Create one 4-note motif. Bars 1-2 exact, 3-4 sequence, 5-6 inversion, 7 truncate, 8 cadence/rest.

Module I - Thirty-Two-Bar Composition Portfolio Capstone
Bars Piece Starting method Requirement
1-8 Piece A motif-first develop one small melodic identity
9-16 Piece B melody-first same melody, chosen harmonization
17-24 Piece C bass-first bass motion drives harmony
25-32 Piece D rhythm-first groove identity drives form
Create four independent eight-bar originals. Each must have a title/working label, one-sentence identity statement, lead sheet, performance arrangement, and
recorded take.

Module J - Revision and Authorship Audit
Question Action
What is the piece's smallest recognizable identity? circle it
Which bar is weakest? rewrite only that bar first
Which note/chord is unnecessary? remove it
Where is the climax? make only that area strongest
Does bar 8 close or continue? choose intentionally
Can the piece survive 50% fewer notes? test reduction
Does it sound like an exercise? add contrast or asymmetry with purpose
Can you perform it from memory? if no, simplify identity
Pass Level 100: 14/16 or better across identity, development, harmony, melody/bass relationship, rhythm, form, revision, and performance. No zero in identity,
development, form, or performance.
Next: Level 101 develops larger form: A/B sections, verse/chorus contrast, bridges, transitions, thematic return, and 16-32 bar original composition.
Fixed roadmap: 100-104 Composition; 105 Final Musicianship Capstone. HARD STOP after Level 105.

This level does not ask for fast eighth- or sixteenth-note strumming. It establishes clean chord formation and changes at whole, half, and quarter notes. Level 50 will expand transition timing and
common-finger movement; later levels add barre chords, triads, CAGED, harmony, and sixteenth-note comping.

Fretting-hand setup Picking-hand setup
Place fingertips just behind the fret wire, not on top of it. Begin on the printed bass string; do not sweep across muted lower strings.
Keep the thumb relaxed behind the neck; do not clamp the palm to the neck. Use shallow pick depth and a relaxed wrist.
Allow open strings enough space beneath curved fingers. Strum through the active string group, then stop the motion.
Form the entire shape before adding unnecessary squeeze. For audits, pick one string at a time with equal volume.
A chord diagram shows where to place the fingers. The exercise is not complete until the correct strings ring, the excluded strings remain silent, and the chord can release without the hand leaving the
fretboard.

steps.safety: Sweep and hybrid practice uses minimum pick depth and relaxed finger extension. Stop for pain or persistent tension.
steps.stop_immediately: Pain, burning tension, uncontrolled string noise, or a collapsing pick grip ends the set immediately.
steps.muting: Fretting hand releases the completed string. Picking-hand palm or spare fingers silence lower strings. The active note should be the only sustained pitch unless a printed pedal tone is intentional.

steps.source_rule: Use one continuous pick motion across the three strings, repeat the highest note with the first upstroke, and reverse. The fretting hand releases each completed string before the next attack.

steps.source_caption: 6-note mirror. Rest after every complete burst.

steps.failure_rule: Failure signs: the three notes sound together, the pick stops between strings, or the top turnaround is late. Repair with a slower one-way three-note sweep before restoring the mirror.

source_session_duties.exact_text: Choose one crosspicking cell, one hybrid cell, and one sweep burst. Stop before fatigue changes the attack. Complete all four endurance circuits for 30 clean seconds with equal rest. Execute all three- and four-string sweep bursts without note overlap. Perform both sixteen-bar capstones without losing the key sequence. Perform every four-system comparison at one stable tempo. Record major and minor performances with intentional system choice and successful recovery. Play all twelve major/minor progression routes with the assigned systems.

manual_execution_contract.source_rule: Begin with one written circuit. When it is clean, repeat continuously for 15 seconds, then rest 15 seconds. Progress to 30 and 60 seconds only when the final repetition matches the first.

instructions.finger_plucks_snap: lower pick volume; reduce finger extension
instructions.sweep_notes_overlap: shorten fret duration; one-way burst only

tempo_advance_gate.exact_text: Add time before tempo. Add tempo only after the longest current block is clean on two days.

source_session_duties.exact_text: Choose one crosspicking cell, one hybrid cell, and one sweep burst. Stop before fatigue changes the attack. Rest at least as long as the work interval during endurance training. A faster phrase is not successful if notes overlap, skipped strings ring, or the chord identity disappears.

source_required_practice_duty.full_gate_text: Complete all crosspicking and hybrid cells with equal tone and both pick starts. Complete all four endurance circuits for 30 clean seconds with equal rest. Execute all three- and four-string sweep bursts without note overlap. Perform both sixteen-bar capstones without losing the key sequence. Perform every four-system comparison at one stable tempo. Record major and minor performances with intentional system choice and successful recovery. Play all twelve major/minor progression routes with the assigned systems.

manual_execution_contract.P_direction_policy: First P is selected D in printed practice and U in opposite practice. Later P directions are explicit learner choices. Fixed sweep/reverse strokes are preserved; only cross/hybrid starts change in I4.

exact_unit_lines: MODULE F - THREE-CHORUS CONTROLLED IMPROVISATION SYNTHESIS
CHORUS 1 - SKELETON AND SPACE
Use P1 and P2 only. Maximum 3 sounding tones per bar. Land one strong target on every chord change and leave at
least one complete beat of silence in every two-bar pair. No D* or G#*.
CHORUS 2 - MOTIF DEVELOPMENT AND POSITION MOVEMENT
Choose one seed motif from Module C. Use one response transformation per two-bar pair. Move through at least four
positions, cross at least two seams, and use no more than one articulation in each two-bar phrase.
CHORUS 3 - FREE SYNTHESIS
Use all five positions and horizontal lanes. Preserve strong beat-1 targets, include at least two bars of deliberate
space, use D* and G#* only on their supporting chords, and finish on an A root without a last-second fret search.

exact_unit_lines: MODULE K - THREE-CHORUS CONTROLLED IMPROVISATION CAPSTONE
CHORUS 1 - MINOR-CENTERED SPACE
Use A minor pentatonic only. Maximum four sounding tones per bar. Use no more than two positions. Leave at
least one full beat of silence in every two-bar pair. Make bars 5 and 9 audible through D or E targets.
CHORUS 2 - BLUES VOCABULARY AND MOTIF DEVELOPMENT
Add Eb, slides, legato, bends, releases, and vibrato. Choose one seed motif and transform it in every two-bar
pair. Move through at least four positions. Use no more than one conspicuous articulation per bar.
CHORUS 3 - CHORD-AWARE COLOR SYNTHESIS
Mix major and minor pentatonic color. Target C# over A7, F# or C over D7, and G#/B/D/E over E7. Use all
five positions, include a dynamic climax, and choose either a tonic close or a functional E7 turnaround.

source_payload.txt_excerpt:
Guitar Exercises - Section VII, Level 60
NEXT: CHORD-TONE SOLOING
Practice progression, error diagnosis, mastery gate, and log
THE PICK MAY MOVE THROUGH FOUR STRINGS; THE NOTES MAY NEVER BECOME A FOUR-STRING STRUM
Ten-phase progression Error diagnosis
1. Silent root/quality commands 6. Seven-note pick-cycle loops NOTES OVERLAP release each fretting finger as the next string sounds
SWEEP RUSHES return to one note per click and stop after every string
2. Low-E-root maj7 and 7 7. Guide-tone accents and ladders
QUALITY UNCLEAR say the seventh and fifth quality before playing
3. Low-E-root m7 and m7b5 8. Major ii-V-I cells
m7b5 SOUNDS LIKE m7 accent the b5 and compare it to the perfect fifth
4. A-root four qualities 9. Minor iiø-V-i cells GUIDE TONES HIDDEN reduce root/fifth volume and accent third/seventh
PICK RESET air-pick the complete 8- or 7-note cycle
5. Alternate/economy comparison 10. Scale links, Q/A, and capstones
TENSION shorten to two strings and reduce 4-6 BPM
Mastery gate before Level 61
Form and spell all 56 root/quality/family commands without sounding them.
Perform all 56 blocked-plus-arpeggiated natural-root shapes.
Use alternate and economy picking without overlapping strings.
Maintain the stroke cycle through all eight seven-note loop cells.
Accent guide tones and complete both same-root quality ladders.
Track six major ii-V-I and six minor iiø-V-i progressions.
Complete all six arpeggio-to-scale links and eight call/answer pairs.
Perform both sixteen-bar capstones on two separate days.
Practice log
Date Module / chord ALT/ECO BPM Clean? Weak crossing / quality Next target
NEXT Level 61 connects seventh-chord arpeggios to chord-tone soloing, approach notes, enclosures, and progression-specific phrase construction.
Standard tuning. Four-string seventh-chord arpeggios. Release each string before the next note sounds. Page 20 of 20

Guitar Exercises - Section VII, Level 61
NEXT: FULL-NECK ARPEGGIO CONNECTION
Practice progression, error diagnosis, mastery gate, and log
THE TARGET MUST REMAIN AUDIBLE AFTER THE APPROACH NOTE IS REMOVED
Ten-phase practice progression Error diagnosis
1. Target rotations 6. Major ii-V-I phrases TARGET HIDDEN LATE RESOLUTION
remove the approach; sustain target alone loop tension-target at half speed
2. Chromatic approaches 7. Minor iiø-V-i phrases
APPROACH TOO LOUD BARLINE LOST
3. Diatonic approaches 8. Five-zone phrases
shorten and soften the non-chord note return to four quarter-note chord tones
4. Enclosures 9. Motif/recovery work
ENCLOSURE RANDOM CHROMATIC SOUP
name the target before notes 1-2 use only one approach event per target
5. Delayed resolutions 10. Model solos and capstones
Mastery gate before Level 62
Complete all sixteen chord-tone target rotations and all twenty-four approach cells. Play all five C-major zone phrases and create one response in an adjacent zone.
Play all sixteen enclosure cells and twelve delayed resolutions without losing the subdivision. Transform the seed motif in six ways and use all twelve recovery cards without stopping the form.
Perform six major and six minor progression phrases in their printed registers. Perform both twelve-bar model solos and both sixteen-bar capstones on two separate days.
Practice log
Date Module / key Target Approach type D/U BPM Clean? Next repair
NEXT Level 62 connects arpeggio fragments diagonally across the neck with string skipping, position shifts, and full-neck chord-tone motif development.
Standard tuning. Chord-tone soloing, approaches, enclosures, delayed resolution, and progression-specific phrasing. Page 20 of 20

Guitar Exercises - Section VII, Level 61
TARGET -> APPROACH -> RESOLUTION
Target hierarchy, approach directions, enclosure formulas, and timing
A CHROMATIC NOTE IS CORRECT ONLY WHEN ITS DESTINATION AND TIMING ARE CLEAR
Target hierarchy
Quality Chord tones Primary phrase targets Color boundary
maj7 R 3 5 7 3 and 7; root for closure 4 and b7 need context
7 R 3 5 b7 3 and b7 11 and 13 are motion unless sustained intentionally
m7 R b3 5 b7 b3 and b7 9 and 11 are open colors
m7b5 R b3 b5 b7 b3, b5, and b7 perfect 5 changes the quality
Approach formulas Enclosure formulas
CHROM BELOW target-1 fret -> target ABOVE-BELOW-TARGET-TARGET
CHROM ABOVE target+1 fret -> target BELOW-ABOVE-TARGET-TARGET
DIATONIC BELOW adjacent scale tone -> target DIATONIC ABOVE + CHROM BELOW + TARGET
DIATONIC ABOVE adjacent scale tone -> target CHROM ABOVE + DIATONIC BELOW + TARGET
DOUBLE reference -> below -> T -> above -> T
The final repeated target proves the pitch center.
Delayed-resolution grid
Count|1---&---2---&---3---&---4---&---|
Role |TENSION-TARGET-CHORD-TARGET-------|
Rule |keep beat 1; resolve by & of 1 or beat 2; leave later space|
Standard tuning. Chord-tone soloing, approaches, enclosures, delayed resolution, and progression-specific phrasing. Page 2 of 20

Guitar Exercises - Section VII, Level 62
NEXT: ADVANCED ARPEGGIO PICKING AND HYBRID SYSTEMS
Practice progression, mastery gate, completion audit, and log
ADVANCE WHEN THE FULL-NECK MOVEMENT IS AUDIBLE AS HARMONY, NOT AS FRETBOARD TRAVEL
Ten-phase practice progression Error diagnosis
1. Preview destinations silently. 6. Inversion-start chains. SKIPPED STRING RINGS reduce pick depth and mute with both hands
SHIFT ARRIVES LATE preview target; move during the previous duration
2. Diagonal triad fragments. 7. Major diagonal cadences.
CHORD IDENTITY LOST return to four chord tones in one position
3. Seventh-chord routes. 8. Minor diagonal cadences.
PICK CYCLE RESETS air-pick through the shift before sounding it
4. String-skip cells. 9. Motif transformations.
MOTIF DISAPPEARS preserve rhythm or role schedule; change one variable
5. Octave shift landings. 10. Capstones and recovery bridges. REGISTER JUMP RANDOM connect with a common role or repeated target
Mastery gate before Level 63
Complete all eight diagonal triad fragments and six seventh-chord routes with both pick starts. Transform the seed motif in eight recognizable ways.
Execute all string-skip and octave-shift cells without unwanted glissando or skipped-string contact. Complete both sixteen-bar capstones without resetting the pick cycle or losing the key sequence.
Identify the starting inversion in all eight inversion chains. Use all recovery cards and at least three bridge templates without stopping the form.
Perform all six major and six minor diagonal progression routes.
Completion audit and practice log
8 triad diagonals 6 seventh routes 8 skip cells 8 shift cells
8 inversion chains 12 cadence routes 8 motif transforms 2 capstones
Date Focus D/U BPM Clean? Weak shift / skip / role Next target
NEXT Level 63 develops crosspicking, hybrid picking, controlled sweep bursts, and arpeggio-based phrase endurance.
Standard tuning. Diagonal arpeggio connections, string skipping, position shifts, and full-neck motif development. Page 20 of 20

source_payload.txt_excerpt:
Guitar Exercises - Section VII, Level 62
PREVIEW -> RELEASE -> RELOCATE -> LAND
Full-neck connection atlas, shift mechanics, and picking rules
THE DESTINATION IS PART OF THE CURRENT NOTE
Five connection zones Shift timing
1. Hear and name the target.
Zone Fret area Primary job
2. Look at the target fret.
Z1 0-5 open/low fragment
3. Release excess pressure.
Z2 5-9 lower-position connection 4. Move thumb and hand together.
5. Land from the bass side or treble side as printed.
Z3 9-13 middle register
6. Re-articulate cleanly; no scrape unless / or \ is marked.
Z4 13-17 upper register
Z5 17-20 high-register destination
String-skip mechanics Picking choices
The pick leaves the current string and travels directly to the destination string. The skipped Adjacent strings: alternate or controlled economy.
string remains silent. Reduce pick depth, pre-locate the destination, and mute unused strings
with both hands. Skipped strings: independent pick attacks.
Odd-note loops: starting stroke reverses next repetition.
Long shifts: preserve the stroke cycle through the move.
FAILURE sweep noise, delayed landing, or a visible search for the next string Muted preview: air-pick the route before sounding it.
Full-neck role map
Chord Low fragment Middle fragment Upper fragment High destination
Cmaj7 C-E-G-B E-G-B-C G-B-C-E B-C-E-G
Dm7 D-F-A-C F-A-C-D A-C-D-F C-D-F-A
G7 G-B-D-F B-D-F-G D-F-G-B F-G-B-D
Am7 A-C-E-G C-E-G-A E-G-A-C G-A-C-E
Standard tuning. Diagonal arpeggio connections, string skipping, position shifts, and full-neck motif development. Page 2 of 20

the usable endurance limit.

source_payload.txt_excerpt:
Four-pass orchestration
1. One system for the complete capstone.
2. Printed four-system rotation.
3. Choose systems by register: pick low, hybrid middle, sweep high.
4. Choose systems by phrase job: crosspick question, hybrid answer, sweep climax.
Recovery cards
Crosspick catches string -> simplify to three-note roll
Hybrid finger misses -> continue with pick-only target
Sweep overlaps -> stop burst on highest clean note
Pick cycle lost -> use next target as new downstroke
Fatigue appears -> insert full-beat rest and reduce density

source_payload.txt_excerpt:
Guitar Exercises - Section VII, Level 63
REUSE THE CAPSTONES | NO EXTRA WRITTEN TONES
Full-performance orchestration, recovery, and phrase-shape control
THE PICKING SYSTEM SUPPORTS THE PHRASE; IT DOES NOT BECOME THE PHRASE
Four-pass orchestration Dynamic and density arc
1. One system for the complete capstone. Bars 1-4: p and sparse. Bars 5-8: mp with one repeated roll. Bars 9-12: mf with wider register.
Bars 13-15: f with one sweep climax. Bar 16: return to mp and release completely.
2. Printed four-system rotation.
3. Choose systems by register: pick low, hybrid middle, sweep high.
4. Choose systems by phrase job: crosspick question, hybrid answer, sweep climax.
Recovery cards Phrase-construction limits
Crosspick catches string -> simplify to three-note roll Use no more than two picking systems inside one four-bar phrase. Keep one recognizable
arpeggio contour. Land on a chord tone at every harmonic change. Leave at least one full-beat
Hybrid finger misses -> continue with pick-only target rest per four bars.
Sweep overlaps -> stop burst on highest clean note
Pick cycle lost -> use next target as new downstroke
Fatigue appears -> insert full-beat rest and reduce density
Final recorded assignment
Record one major and one minor sixteen-bar performance. The first take follows the printed systems. The second chooses systems by musical function. Evaluate tone equality, note separation, muting,
tempo, chord identity, dynamic shape, and recovery.
PASS The second performance must sound more musical, not merely more technically varied.
Standard tuning. Crosspicking, hybrid picking, controlled sweep bursts, and arpeggio phrase endurance. Page 19 of 20

task.label: Silent-formation audit
task.instructions:
Guitar Exercises - Section VI, Level 52
42 SILENT PROMPTS + EAR TASKS
Module J - inversion hearing, degree identification, and random-root recovery
NAME THE THREE DEGREES BEFORE USING THE SHAPE AS A CHORD
Inversion-recognition cards Six random-root commands
1-3-5 major root position 1. Find a named root-position major triad.
3-5-1 major first inversion 2. Move to first inversion without changing quality.
5-1-3 major second inversion 3. Move to second inversion and name the bass voice.
1-b3-5 minor root position 4. Convert major to minor by moving one string.
5. Arpeggiate G-B-e-e-B-G and sing the degrees.
b3-5-1 minor first inversion
6. Find the nearest inversion of the next I-IV-V chord.
5-1-b3 minor second inversion
Ear-training passes
A. Play major then minor at the same inversion; identify the moving third by ear.
B. Play all three inversions of one chord in random order; name the bass role.
C. Sing root-third-fifth, then play the matching blocked triad.
D. Sustain one common note while moving the other two voices through I-IV-V-I.
E. Record a progression and identify which string carries the melody.
Silent-formation audit
Draw a random natural root, quality, and inversion. State the spelling and G-B-e degree order; look at the destination; form the triad silently; release; then verify with one blocked attack. Complete all 42
combinations over multiple sessions.
PASS At least 18 of 21 shapes per quality are formed correctly on the first attempt.
Major and minor triads on G-B-e: root position, first inversion, second inversion. Use minimum pressure. Page 19 of 20

- Map all seven natural roots as major and minor triads on all four adjacent string sets.
- Identify all three inversions from the lowest sounding voice.
- Complete C/Cm and G/Gm set transfers without leakage.
- Switch quality in all twelve set/inversion combinations by moving one voice.
- Perform all eight progressions and both sixteen-bar capstones.
- Use blocked, arpeggiated, release, top-voice, bass-voice, and melodic-fragment patterns.
- Pass at least 30 of 42 random prompts per string-set family on the first attempt.

Guitar Exercises - Section VII, Level 64
NEXT: HARMONIC MINOR
Section VII mastery gate, performance orchestration, and practice log
THE CAPSTONE IS COMPLETE WHEN THE SOLO SOUNDS DESIGNED ACROSS MULTIPLE KEYS
Ten-phase practice progression Performance orchestration test
1. Five phrase-architecture cells 6. Eight system-aware phrases Take 1: use the printed systems. Sweep only at a planned climax.
2. Five secondary-dominant resolutions 7. Four eight-bar studies
Take 2: choose by phrase function. Alternate-pick after an error.
3. Five guide-tone cells 8. Major capstone
4. Four major key changes 9. Minor capstone Keep one system for a full bar. Record the key-center / arc audit.
5. Four minor key changes 10. Recovery and bridge templates
Mastery gate and Section VII completion standard
Resolve all five secondary dominants to the correct destination chord. Recover from a missed note or system error without abandoning the key sequence.
Perform all major and minor key-change routes without a form pause. Record one major and one minor long-form solo whose phrase arc is audible to a listener.
Use all five picking systems without changing the written rhythm or harmony. Meet the complete standard on two separate days.
Perform the four eight-bar studies and both sixteen-bar capstones.
Practice log and next section
Date Study / key change System BPM Clean? Weak harmony / phrase / system Next target
NEXT Section VIII begins with harmonic minor: leading-tone control, V7 and vii° harmony, and minor-key arpeggio application.
Long-form arpeggio solo construction, secondary dominants, key changes, and picking-system orchestration. Page 20 of 20

Guitar Exercises - Section VIII, Level 65
NEXT: FIVE-POSITION HARMONIC-MINOR MAP
Practice progression, mastery gate, completion audit, and log
ADVANCE ONLY WHEN G#, E7, AND THE DIMINISHED CHORDS HAVE CLEAR MUSICAL FUNCTIONS
Ten-phase practice progression Error diagnosis
1. Natural / harmonic comparison 6. Five melodic cells G# OPTIONAL sing 7-1; sustain A longer
F-G# RUSHES loop E-F-G#-A slowly
2. Three octave routes 7. Seven triad arpeggios
Em / E BLUR isolate G versus G#
3. Two-octave mirror 8. v / V / V7 comparison
DIM ROOT LOST name G# before the shape
4. Leading-tone cells 9. Diminished resolutions
G# OVERUSED limit it to its stated function
5. Augmented-second cells 10. Five phrases + model forms PICK RESET air-pick the mirror count
Mastery gate before Level 66
Formula, leading tone, and augmented second v, V, and V7 by ear and execution
All comparison and octave routes G#dim and G#dim7 in five registers
All leading-tone and augmented-second cells Five cadence phrases plus both model forms on two days
Seven harmonized-triad arpeggios
Completion audit and practice log
6 compare cells 3 octave cells 2-octave route 6 leading cells 6 aug2 cells
7 triad arps 3 dominant cells 10 diminished cells 5 zone phrases model + capstone
Date Focus D/U BPM Clean? Weak interval / chord Next target
Standard tuning. Fixed key: A harmonic minor. Raised seventh G#; augmented second F-G#. Page 20 of 20

source_payload.txt_excerpt:
Guitar Exercises - Section VIII, Level 66
NEXT: HARMONIC-MINOR SEQUENCES AND MODE FUNCTIONS
Practice progression, recovery rules, mastery gate, and log
ADVANCE ONLY WHEN G#-A, F-G#, THE SEAMS, AND THE FULL-REGISTER ROUTE REMAIN CONTROLLED
Ten-phase practice progression Error diagnosis and recovery
1. Name all five frames and starting degrees. 6. Play the five printed sequence patterns. LOST FRAME name the low-E start degree and fret span
EARLY SHIFT stay through the final shared note; move after it
2. Complete P1 with notes and degrees. 7. Complete forward and reverse zigzags.
AUG2 COLLAPSE play F, sing G#, relocate, then land
3. Add P2-P5, one frame per session. 8. Match all characteristic-tone cells.
WEAK LEADING TONE hold G#, then resolve to A without rushing
4. Learn all four shared-anchor seams. 9. Play all four seam phrases. PICK RESET air-pick the 18-, 36-, 42-, or 90-tone count
RINGING STRING reduce pressure and mute before the destination
5. Map all six horizontal lanes. 10. Perform the sixteen-bar capstone twice.
FORM LOSS return to one chord-tone target per bar
Mastery gate before Level 67
Name every frame, fret span, low-E start degree, and printed A root. Perform forward and reverse 90-tone zigzags on two separate days.
Play all five 36-tone cells with both alternate-picking starts. Distinguish G#-A from G-A and preserve every F-G# augmented second.
Complete all four seams twice without scrape, pause, or pick reset. Play all seam phrases and the sixteen-bar capstone from memory.
Play all six horizontal lanes and all five sequence patterns.
Completion audit and practice log
5 position cells 4 seam cells 6 lanes 5 sequence cells
2 zigzags 10 characteristic cells 4 seam phrases 16-bar capstone
Date Module / position D/U BPM Clean? Weak seam / tone / route Next target
NEXT Level 67 develops harmonic-minor interval sequences, arpeggio overlays, and progression-specific melodic applications.
Standard tuning. Fixed key: A harmonic minor. Core register: frets 5-17; selected leading-tone extensions to fret 19. Page 20 of 20

Guitar Exercises - Section VIII, Level 67
ADVANCE BY FUNCTIONAL HEARING, NOT MODE-NAME RECALL
Practice progression, error diagnosis, mastery gate, and log
THE MODE IS CORRECT ONLY WHEN THE CHORD AND RESOLUTION ARE AUDIBLE
Ten-phase practice progression Error diagnosis
1. P1 thirds, fourths, fifths, and sixths. 6. Seven mode-function cells. MODE NAME WITHOUT FUNCTION hold the chord or drone and stop on its root
INTERVAL RUN BECOMES SCALE remove the connecting notes; play only the pair
2. Translate each interval type through P2-P5. 7. Five i-iv-V7-i phrases.
AUG2 RUSH isolate F-G# and keep equal subdivisions
3. Seven triad overlays. 8. Three alternate progression families. V7 SOUNDS MINOR accent G# before adding F or C color
DIMINISHED CELL SOUNDS RANDOM state G#dim7, then resolve every voice
4. Seven seventh-chord overlays. 9. Five E Phrygian dominant cells.
III+ SOUNDS UNSTABLE land C-E-G# first; add B only after the triad is clear
5. Seven mode mirrors over sustained chords. 10. Characteristic resolutions and capstone. FORM LOSS return to quarter-note chord tones and name each bar
Mastery gate before Level 68
Play all twenty interval cells and identify the diatonic interval family by ear. Complete five i-iv-V7-i phrases and all three alternate progression families.
Spell and arpeggiate all seven triads and seven seventh chords. Perform E Phrygian dominant in five registers and resolve every cell to A minor.
Perform all seven mode mirrors while the local chord remains audible. Complete all five characteristic chord-resolution cells and the sixteen-bar capstone.
Play all seven function cells and explain the characteristic color.
Practice log
Date Module / mode Chord function D/U BPM Clean? Weak interval / resolution Next target
NEXT Level 68: E Phrygian dominant, diminished-seventh symmetry, altered dominant colors, and harmonic-minor improvisation synthesis.
Standard tuning. Fixed key: A harmonic minor. Mode names describe harmonic function, not seven unrelated box systems. Page 20 of 20

Guitar Exercises - Section VIII, Level 68
HARMONIC MINOR SECTION COMPLETE
Section VIII mastery gate, completion audit, and practice log
ADVANCE AFTER TWO CLEAN DAYS WITH AUDIBLE DOMINANT FUNCTION AND TONIC RESOLUTION
Mastery gate
Play E Phrygian dominant in all five positions and name every E7 role. Complete all six dominant tension cells and distinguish b9, #9*, 11, and b13 by ear.
Play all five E7b9 mirrors and extract the G#dim7 upper structure. Move the diminished shape through all four minor-third positions without note overlap.
Resolve every diminished inversion to A minor and explain G#dim7 function. Complete all five i-iv-V7-i and iiø-V7-i phrases.
Perform all five call/response pairs and the sixteen-bar model solo. Record all three capstone passes without losing form or overusing borrowed G.
Completion audit Section VIII listening standard
5 mode mirrors 6 tension cells A listener should hear Am as tonic, E7 as the dominant, G# as the leading tone, F as b9 color, C as
b13 color, and G#dim7 as a functional upper structure rather than an isolated symmetrical pattern.
5 E7b9 mirrors 4 diminished shapes
4 diminished resolutions 10 cadence phrases
5 call/response pairs 16-bar solo
Practice log
Date Module Position / chord D/U BPM Clean? Weak tension / resolution Next target
NEXT Section IX begins with A melodic minor: raised sixth and seventh, minor-major tonic color, and new seventh-chord harmony.
Standard tuning. A harmonic minor / E Phrygian dominant. Starred colors are borrowed or function-specific. Page 20 of 20

Guitar Exercises - Section IX, Level 69
CONSTRUCTION BEFORE SPEED
Practice progression, error diagnosis, and workload audit
REPAIR THE FIRST FAILED PITCH DECISION, NOT THE LAST WRONG NOTE
Ten-phase practice progression Error diagnosis
1. Six upper-tetrachord comparisons. F LEAKS INTO ASCENT isolate F-F#-G#-A
2. Three octave routes and the two-octave mirror.
G LEAKS INTO SYMMETRIC DESCENT reverse the melodic ascent slowly
3. Three classical directional cells.
4. Six raised-sixth cells. CLASSICAL DESCENT SOUNDS FORCED delay the switch until after the phrase peak
5. Six raised-seventh cells.
D7 SOUNDS LIKE Dm7 accent F# before C
6. Seven triads and seven seventh chords.
7. Four tonic-color cells. Bm7 SOUNDS DIMINISHED establish F# as the fifth
8. Five progression phrases.
TONIC SOUNDS MAJOR sustain C before G# or F# color
9. Eight-bar model and sixteen-bar capstone.
FORM LOSS return to quarter-note chord tones
10. Recovery cards and improvisation passes.
Written workload audit
A - three forms 72 F - triads 56 Advancement: add 2 BPM after three clean repetitions at the current route length.
If the wrong sixth or seventh appears twice, reduce the route to one tetrachord
B - octave routes 78 G - sevenths 70 before changing tempo.
C - raised sixth 48 H - tonic colors 32
D - raised seventh 36 I - progressions 80
E - direction options 48 J - model/capstone 120
TOTAL WRITTEN TONES: 640
Listening assignment
Record the natural, harmonic, and melodic upper tetrachords without announcing them. Identify them by ear the next day. Repeat with one symmetric and one classical descent.
Standard tuning. Fixed key: A melodic minor. Classical and symmetric descending options are labeled separately. Page 19 of 20

RIGID STRETCH release and reform instead of clamping the full span

Practice log

Scale Exercises - Section IX, Level 71
NEXT: LYDIAN DOMINANT AND ALTERED-DOMINANT SYNTHESIS
Practice progression, error diagnosis, mastery gate, and log
NAME THE CHORD, MODE, CHARACTERISTIC NOTE, AND DESTINATION
Ten-phase practice progression Error diagnosis
1. One interval family in P1 6. Mode-function cells MODE WITHOUT CHORD return to the arpeggio and drone
LOST #4 isolate D-F#-G#-A over D7
2. All intervals in one position 7. Five cadence phrases
LOST b6 isolate B-C-D-E over E7
3. Triad overlays 8. Alternate progressions
ALTERED SOUP play G#-C-F# first; add one alteration
WRONG MODE 7 NAME state destination: A minor or C# minor
4. Seventh overlays 9. D Lydian dominant routes
INTERVAL FRET SEARCH name both notes before moving
5. Seven mode mirrors 10. Resolutions and capstone
PICK RESET air-pick the complete twelve-tone cell
Mastery gate before Level 72

Play and name all seven modes with the correct chord function. Perform the sixteen-bar capstone on two separate days without losing the mode-function labels.
Perform the five iMaj7-IV7-V7-iMaj7 phrases and all three alternate progressions.
Practice log
Date Module / mode Chord function D/U BPM Clean? Weak interval / color Next target

source_payload.txt_excerpt:
Guitar Exercises - Section VI, Level 57
A7-D7-E7 | LOW / MIDDLE / HIGH
Module G - A-blues dominant shell map in three registers
SHELLS REDUCE PRESSURE AND LEAVE ROOM FOR THE LEAD VOCABULARY FROM SECTION V
Use root-inclusive shells in the low register and rootless guide-tone dyads in the middle and high registers. Name the third and flat seventh before every chord change.
Low register - root-inclusive shells
A7 D7 E7
Str|E---A---D---G---B---e---| Str|E---A---D---G---B---e---| Str|E---A---D---G---B---e---|
Fre|5 x 5 6 x x | Fre|x 5 x 5 7 x | Fre|x 7 x 7 9 x |
Nte|A x G C# x x | Nte|x D x C F# x | Nte|x E x D G# x |
Rol|R x b7 3 x x | Rol|x R x b7 3 x | Rol|x R x b7 3 x |
Middle rootless dyads - D/G High rootless dyads - B/e
Chord Lower Upper Roles Chord Lower Upper Roles
A7 D11 G12 3 + b7 A7 B14 e15 3 + b7
D7 D10 G11 b7 + 3 D7 B13 e14 b7 + 3
E7 D12 G13 b7 + 3 E7 B15 e16 b7 + 3
Register connection
Bars 1-4: low shells. Bars 5-8: middle dyads. Bars 9-12: high dyads. The chord identity must remain equally clear when the root is removed. Add a bass root only when the ensemble needs it.
Standard tuning. Seventh chords, shell voicings, ii-V-I movement, and functional voice leading. Page 15 of 20

source_payload.label: Quality-identification loop
parent_path: Ear training, random-quality commands, and error-repair laboratory
source_payload.txt_excerpt:
Quality-identification loop
Record maj7, 7, m7, and m7b5 at the same root in random order. Identify the quality, the altered
voice, and whether the seventh is major or minor before checking the fretboard.
Random command cards
G7 E-root Cmaj7 A-root
Bm7 A-root Em7b5 E-root

Phrase architecture hierarchy Picking-system function map
Layer Question System Best use
Harmony What chord or temporary tonic is active? Alternate chromatic links, recovery, neutral connection
Motif What remains recognizable? Economy linear arpeggio launch
Register Where is the phrase moving? Crosspick repeating question or rolling motif
Rhythm Where is the space? Hybrid bass plus upper-voice answer

E -> F 5 -> b6 half step
F -> G# b6 -> 7 augmented second
G# -> A 7 -> 1 half step

Mode Name Formula Chord function Characteristic color

source_payload.txt_excerpt:
Guitar Exercises - Section IX, Level 69
REUSE THE WRITTEN TARGETS; CHANGE ONE VARIABLE AT A TIME
Melodic-minor improvisation laboratory
THE SCALE FORM IS A CHOICE; THE CHORD TARGET AND BARLINE ARE FIXED
Use the progression | AmMaj7 | D7 | E7 | AmMaj7 |. The five passes below reuse the same beat-one target schedule and gradually reduce the written support.
Pass 1 - chord tones only One root, third, fifth, or seventh per beat. No scale connectors.
Pass 2 - melodic-minor connectors Add F# and G# as scale motion while preserving every target.
Pass 3 - symmetric descent Use A melodic minor in both directions.
Pass 4 - classical descent Ascend with F#/G#; descend with F/G after the tonic or phrase peak.
Pass 5 - tonic-color answer Answer the final AmMaj7 phrase with Am6 or Am6/9 color.
STOP RULE If F/F# or G/G# changes without intention, return to one color pair and one bar.
Standard tuning. Fixed key: A melodic minor. Classical and symmetric descending options are labeled separately. Page 18 of 20

source_payload.txt_excerpt:
Scale Exercises - Section IX, Level 71
CHORD FIRST | MODE SECOND | DESTINATION THIRD
Mode/function atlas and seventh-mode dual interpretation
SEVEN MODES SHARE ONE PITCH COLLECTION BUT DO NOT SHARE ONE FUNCTION
Degree Mode Formula Primary chord function
1 A melodic minor 1 2 b3 4 5 6 7 AmMaj7 / iMaj7
2 B Dorian b2 1 b2 b3 4 5 6 b7 Bm7 / ii7
3 C Lydian augmented 1 2 3 #4 #5 6 7 Cmaj7#5 / IIImaj7#5
4 D Lydian dominant 1 2 3 #4 5 6 b7 D7#11 / IV7
5 E Mixolydian b6 1 2 3 4 5 b6 b7 E7b13 / V7
6 F# Locrian natural 2 1 2 b3 4 b5 b6 b7 F#m7b5 / vi-half-dim
7 G# altered 1 b9 #9 3 b5 #5 b7 G#7alt applied dominant; parent stack G#m7b5
Parent-key reading Applied altered-dominant reading
Stacking diatonic thirds on scale degree 7 produces G#-B-D-F#: G#m7b5. In the parent A-minor When G# is treated as a dominant root, C is respelled B# as the major third. The same pitch
system, it can resolve by half-step motion into AmMaj7. collection becomes G# altered and points toward C# major or minor.
PRACTICE ORDER Chord arpeggio -> one-octave mode -> characteristic note -> destination chord.
WARNING Do not apply altered-scale tension to G#m7b5 unless the harmony has actually been reinterpreted as G#7alt.
Standard tuning. Fixed key: A melodic minor. Modes are tied to chord function, not treated as unrelated scale boxes. Page 2 of 20

Scale Exercises - Section IX, Level 72
DIRECT G#7alt | SUBSTITUTE D7#11 | DESTINATION C#m
Dominant-pair atlas, shared tritone, and destination voice leading
THE SAME C-F# TRITONE CHANGES NAME AND RESOLUTION DIRECTION WITH THE ROOT
D7#11 - D Lydian dominant G#7alt - G# altered
Chord tones: D F# A C Chord shell: G# B# F#
Roles: R 3 5 b7 Roles: R 3 b7
Mode colors: E G# B Alterations: A B D E
Roles: 9 #11 13 Roles: b9 #9 b5 #5
Primary motion into C#m: Primary motion into C#m:
D -> C# F# -> E C -> B G# remains common B# -> C# F# -> E A -> G# E remains common
Enharmonic tritone and destination map
Pitch pair Over G#7alt Over D7#11 Resolution into C#m
C / B# and F# 3 and b7 b7 and 3 B#->C# / C->B; F#->E
G# root #11 common tone: fifth of C#m
A b9 5 A->G#
B #9 13 common tone: b7 of C#m
E #5 9 common tone: b3 of C#m
Listening order
1. Play C-F# alone. 2. Add G# below it and hear direct dominant pull. 3. Add D below it and hear the tritone substitute. 4. Resolve both versions to C#m. The shell is shared; the root and voice-leading
direction define the function.
Standard tuning. Parent collection: A melodic minor. Dominant functions are named by chord and destination. Page 2 of 20

Guitar Exercises - Section VI, Level 57
6 KEYS | FUNCTION BEFORE GRIP
Module F - minor iiø-V-i voice leading and m7 versus m7b5 distinction
iiø AND m7 SHARE b3 + b7; THE FLAT FIFTH DEFINES HALF-DIMINISHED QUALITY
The guide-tone dyad alone cannot distinguish iim7b5 from iim7. Hear or add the flat fifth before reducing to the shell. The V chord then supplies the raised seventh that resolves into the minor tonic.
Key iiø-V-i iiø full check D voice G voice
A Bm7b5-E7-Am7 x 2 3 2 3 x 12-12-10 14-13-12
E F#m7b5-B7-Em7 x 9 10 9 10 x 7-7-5 9-8-7
B C#m7b5-F#7-Bm7 x 4 5 4 5 x 14-14-12 16-15-14
F# G#m7b5-C#7-F#m7 x 11 12 11 12 x 9-9-7 11-10-9
C# D#m7b5-G#7-C#m7 x 6 7 6 7 x 16-16-14 18-17-16
D Em7b5-A7-Dm7 x 7 8 7 8 x 17-17-15 19-18-17
Two-stage iiø drill Dominant-resolution drill
1. Play the full four-note m7b5 voicing and sing the b5. 2. Remove the b5 and continue with the Hold the V third, sing the tonic, then resolve both guide voices into the minor i. Do not let the raised
rootless guide-tone dyad. seventh remain as a permanent scale note.
EAR TEST Alternate m7 and m7b5 at the same root. The only changed voice is the fifth.
Standard tuning. Seventh chords, shell voicings, ii-V-I movement, and functional voice leading. Page 14 of 20

SEAM P1-P2
E: frets 5-7-8-10-8-7-5 | notes A-B-C-D-C-B-A | degrees 1-2-b3-4-b3-2-1
A: frets 5-7-8-11-8-7-5 | notes D-E-F-G#-F-E-D | degrees 4-5-b6-7-b6-5-4
D: frets 6-7-9-10-9-7-6 | notes G#-A-B-C-B-A-G# | degrees 7-1-2-b3-2-1-7
G: frets 5-7-9-10-9-7-5 | notes C-D-E-F-E-D-C | degrees b3-4-5-b6-5-4-b3
B: frets 6-9-10-12-10-9-6 | notes F-G#-A-B-A-G#-F | degrees b6-7-1-2-1-7-b6
e: frets 7-8-10-12-10-8-7 | notes B-C-D-E-D-C-B | degrees 2-b3-4-5-4-b3-2
Count: 6 strings x 7 notes = 42 tones. Repeat twice to restore the original starting stroke.

Guitar Exercises - Section VIII, Level 66
NEXT: HARMONIC-MINOR SEQUENCES AND MODE FUNCTIONS
Practice progression, recovery rules, mastery gate, and log
ADVANCE ONLY WHEN G#-A, F-G#, THE SEAMS, AND THE FULL-REGISTER ROUTE REMAIN CONTROLLED
Ten-phase practice progression Error diagnosis and recovery
1. Name all five frames and starting degrees. 6. Play the five printed sequence patterns. LOST FRAME name the low-E start degree and fret span
EARLY SHIFT stay through the final shared note; move after it
2. Complete P1 with notes and degrees. 7. Complete forward and reverse zigzags.
AUG2 COLLAPSE play F, sing G#, relocate, then land
3. Add P2-P5, one frame per session. 8. Match all characteristic-tone cells.
WEAK LEADING TONE hold G#, then resolve to A without rushing
4. Learn all four shared-anchor seams. 9. Play all four seam phrases. PICK RESET air-pick the 18-, 36-, 42-, or 90-tone count
RINGING STRING reduce pressure and mute before the destination
5. Map all six horizontal lanes. 10. Perform the sixteen-bar capstone twice.
FORM LOSS return to one chord-tone target per bar
Mastery gate before Level 67
Name every frame, fret span, low-E start degree, and printed A root. Perform forward and reverse 90-tone zigzags on two separate days.
Play all five 36-tone cells with both alternate-picking starts. Distinguish G#-A from G-A and preserve every F-G# augmented second.
Complete all four seams twice without scrape, pause, or pick reset. Play all seam phrases and the sixteen-bar capstone from memory.
Play all six horizontal lanes and all five sequence patterns.
Completion audit and practice log
5 position cells 4 seam cells 6 lanes 5 sequence cells
2 zigzags 10 characteristic cells 4 seam phrases 16-bar capstone

source_full_book_mastery.exact_full_page:
Guitar Exercises - Section VIII, Level 67
ADVANCE BY FUNCTIONAL HEARING, NOT MODE-NAME RECALL
Practice progression, error diagnosis, mastery gate, and log
THE MODE IS CORRECT ONLY WHEN THE CHORD AND RESOLUTION ARE AUDIBLE
Ten-phase practice progression Error diagnosis
1. P1 thirds, fourths, fifths, and sixths. 6. Seven mode-function cells. MODE NAME WITHOUT FUNCTION hold the chord or drone and stop on its root
INTERVAL RUN BECOMES SCALE remove the connecting notes; play only the pair
2. Translate each interval type through P2-P5. 7. Five i-iv-V7-i phrases.
AUG2 RUSH isolate F-G# and keep equal subdivisions
3. Seven triad overlays. 8. Three alternate progression families. V7 SOUNDS MINOR accent G# before adding F or C color
DIMINISHED CELL SOUNDS RANDOM state G#dim7, then resolve every voice
4. Seven seventh-chord overlays. 9. Five E Phrygian dominant cells.
III+ SOUNDS UNSTABLE land C-E-G# first; add B only after the triad is clear
5. Seven mode mirrors over sustained chords. 10. Characteristic resolutions and capstone. FORM LOSS return to quarter-note chord tones and name each bar
Mastery gate before Level 68
Play all twenty interval cells and identify the diatonic interval family by ear. Complete five i-iv-V7-i phrases and all three alternate progression families.
Spell and arpeggiate all seven triads and seven seventh chords. Perform E Phrygian dominant in five registers and resolve every cell to A minor.
Perform all seven mode mirrors while the local chord remains audible. Complete all five characteristic chord-resolution cells and the sixteen-bar capstone.
Play all seven function cells and explain the characteristic color.
Practice log
Date Module / mode Chord function D/U BPM Clean? Weak interval / resolution Next target
NEXT Level 68: E Phrygian dominant, diminished-seventh symmetry, altered dominant colors, and harmonic-minor improvisation synthesis.
Standard tuning. Fixed key: A harmonic minor. Mode names describe harmonic function, not seven unrelated box systems. Page 20 of 20

Guitar Exercises - Section VIII, Level 67
ADVANCE BY FUNCTIONAL HEARING, NOT MODE-NAME RECALL
Practice progression, error diagnosis, mastery gate, and log
THE MODE IS CORRECT ONLY WHEN THE CHORD AND RESOLUTION ARE AUDIBLE
Ten-phase practice progression Error diagnosis
1. P1 thirds, fourths, fifths, and sixths. 6. Seven mode-function cells. MODE NAME WITHOUT FUNCTION hold the chord or drone and stop on its root
INTERVAL RUN BECOMES SCALE remove the connecting notes; play only the pair
2. Translate each interval type through P2-P5. 7. Five i-iv-V7-i phrases.
AUG2 RUSH isolate F-G# and keep equal subdivisions
3. Seven triad overlays. 8. Three alternate progression families. V7 SOUNDS MINOR accent G# before adding F or C color
DIMINISHED CELL SOUNDS RANDOM state G#dim7, then resolve every voice
4. Seven seventh-chord overlays. 9. Five E Phrygian dominant cells.
III+ SOUNDS UNSTABLE land C-E-G# first; add B only after the triad is clear
5. Seven mode mirrors over sustained chords. 10. Characteristic resolutions and capstone. FORM LOSS return to quarter-note chord tones and name each bar
Mastery gate before Level 68
Play all twenty interval cells and identify the diatonic interval family by ear. Complete five i-iv-V7-i phrases and all three alternate progression families.
Spell and arpeggiate all seven triads and seven seventh chords. Perform E Phrygian dominant in five registers and resolve every cell to A minor.
Perform all seven mode mirrors while the local chord remains audible. Complete all five characteristic chord-resolution cells and the sixteen-bar capstone.
Play all seven function cells and explain the characteristic color.
Practice log
Date Module / mode Chord function D/U BPM Clean? Weak interval / resolution Next target
NEXT Level 68: E Phrygian dominant, diminished-seventh symmetry, altered dominant colors, and harmonic-minor improvisation synthesis.
Standard tuning. Fixed key: A harmonic minor. Mode names describe harmonic function, not seven unrelated box systems. Page 20 of 20

source_full_book_mastery.exact_full_page:
Guitar Exercises - Section VIII, Level 67
ADVANCE BY FUNCTIONAL HEARING, NOT MODE-NAME RECALL
Practice progression, error diagnosis, mastery gate, and log
THE MODE IS CORRECT ONLY WHEN THE CHORD AND RESOLUTION ARE AUDIBLE
Ten-phase practice progression Error diagnosis
1. P1 thirds, fourths, fifths, and sixths. 6. Seven mode-function cells. MODE NAME WITHOUT FUNCTION hold the chord or drone and stop on its root
INTERVAL RUN BECOMES SCALE remove the connecting notes; play only the pair
2. Translate each interval type through P2-P5. 7. Five i-iv-V7-i phrases.
AUG2 RUSH isolate F-G# and keep equal subdivisions
3. Seven triad overlays. 8. Three alternate progression families. V7 SOUNDS MINOR accent G# before adding F or C color
DIMINISHED CELL SOUNDS RANDOM state G#dim7, then resolve every voice
4. Seven seventh-chord overlays. 9. Five E Phrygian dominant cells.
III+ SOUNDS UNSTABLE land C-E-G# first; add B only after the triad is clear
5. Seven mode mirrors over sustained chords. 10. Characteristic resolutions and capstone. FORM LOSS return to quarter-note chord tones and name each bar
Mastery gate before Level 68
Play all twenty interval cells and identify the diatonic interval family by ear. Complete five i-iv-V7-i phrases and all three alternate progression families.
Spell and arpeggiate all seven triads and seven seventh chords. Perform E Phrygian dominant in five registers and resolve every cell to A minor.
Perform all seven mode mirrors while the local chord remains audible. Complete all five characteristic chord-resolution cells and the sixteen-bar capstone.
Play all seven function cells and explain the characteristic color.
Practice log
Date Module / mode Chord function D/U BPM Clean? Weak interval / resolution Next target
NEXT Level 68: E Phrygian dominant, diminished-seventh symmetry, altered dominant colors, and harmonic-minor improvisation synthesis.
Standard tuning. Fixed key: A harmonic minor. Mode names describe harmonic function, not seven unrelated box systems. Page 20 of 20

Guitar Exercises - Section VIII, Level 67
ADVANCE BY FUNCTIONAL HEARING, NOT MODE-NAME RECALL
Practice progression, error diagnosis, mastery gate, and log
THE MODE IS CORRECT ONLY WHEN THE CHORD AND RESOLUTION ARE AUDIBLE
Ten-phase practice progression Error diagnosis

INTERVAL RUN BECOMES SCALE remove the connecting notes; play only the pair

AUG2 RUSH isolate F-G# and keep equal subdivisions

DIMINISHED CELL SOUNDS RANDOM state G#dim7, then resolve every voice
4. Seven seventh-chord overlays. 9. Five E Phrygian dominant cells.
III+ SOUNDS UNSTABLE land C-E-G# first; add B only after the triad is clear
5. Seven mode mirrors over sustained chords. 10. Characteristic resolutions and capstone. FORM LOSS return to quarter-note chord tones and name each bar

Perform all seven mode mirrors while the local chord remains audible. Complete all five characteristic chord-resolution cells and the sixteen-bar capstone.
Play all seven function cells and explain the characteristic color.

Date Module / mode Chord function D/U BPM Clean? Weak interval / resolution Next target

source_full_book_mastery.exact_full_page:
Guitar Exercises - Section VIII, Level 67
ADVANCE BY FUNCTIONAL HEARING, NOT MODE-NAME RECALL
Practice progression, error diagnosis, mastery gate, and log
THE MODE IS CORRECT ONLY WHEN THE CHORD AND RESOLUTION ARE AUDIBLE
Ten-phase practice progression Error diagnosis
1. P1 thirds, fourths, fifths, and sixths. 6. Seven mode-function cells. MODE NAME WITHOUT FUNCTION hold the chord or drone and stop on its root
INTERVAL RUN BECOMES SCALE remove the connecting notes; play only the pair
2. Translate each interval type through P2-P5. 7. Five i-iv-V7-i phrases.
AUG2 RUSH isolate F-G# and keep equal subdivisions
3. Seven triad overlays. 8. Three alternate progression families. V7 SOUNDS MINOR accent G# before adding F or C color
DIMINISHED CELL SOUNDS RANDOM state G#dim7, then resolve every voice
4. Seven seventh-chord overlays. 9. Five E Phrygian dominant cells.
III+ SOUNDS UNSTABLE land C-E-G# first; add B only after the triad is clear
5. Seven mode mirrors over sustained chords. 10. Characteristic resolutions and capstone. FORM LOSS return to quarter-note chord tones and name each bar
Mastery gate before Level 68
Play all twenty interval cells and identify the diatonic interval family by ear. Complete five i-iv-V7-i phrases and all three alternate progression families.
Spell and arpeggiate all seven triads and seven seventh chords. Perform E Phrygian dominant in five registers and resolve every cell to A minor.
Perform all seven mode mirrors while the local chord remains audible. Complete all five characteristic chord-resolution cells and the sixteen-bar capstone.
Play all seven function cells and explain the characteristic color.
Practice log
Date Module / mode Chord function D/U BPM Clean? Weak interval / resolution Next target
NEXT Level 68: E Phrygian dominant, diminished-seventh symmetry, altered dominant colors, and harmonic-minor improvisation synthesis.
Standard tuning. Fixed key: A harmonic minor. Mode names describe harmonic function, not seven unrelated box systems. Page 20 of 20

Guitar Exercises - Section VIII, Level 67
ADVANCE BY FUNCTIONAL HEARING, NOT MODE-NAME RECALL
Practice progression, error diagnosis, mastery gate, and log
THE MODE IS CORRECT ONLY WHEN THE CHORD AND RESOLUTION ARE AUDIBLE
Ten-phase practice progression Error diagnosis
1. P1 thirds, fourths, fifths, and sixths. 6. Seven mode-function cells. MODE NAME WITHOUT FUNCTION hold the chord or drone and stop on its root
INTERVAL RUN BECOMES SCALE remove the connecting notes; play only the pair
2. Translate each interval type through P2-P5. 7. Five i-iv-V7-i phrases.
AUG2 RUSH isolate F-G# and keep equal subdivisions
3. Seven triad overlays. 8. Three alternate progression families. V7 SOUNDS MINOR accent G# before adding F or C color
DIMINISHED CELL SOUNDS RANDOM state G#dim7, then resolve every voice
4. Seven seventh-chord overlays. 9. Five E Phrygian dominant cells.
III+ SOUNDS UNSTABLE land C-E-G# first; add B only after the triad is clear
5. Seven mode mirrors over sustained chords. 10. Characteristic resolutions and capstone. FORM LOSS return to quarter-note chord tones and name each bar
Mastery gate before Level 68
Play all twenty interval cells and identify the diatonic interval family by ear. Complete five i-iv-V7-i phrases and all three alternate progression families.
Spell and arpeggiate all seven triads and seven seventh chords. Perform E Phrygian dominant in five registers and resolve every cell to A minor.
Perform all seven mode mirrors while the local chord remains audible. Complete all five characteristic chord-resolution cells and the sixteen-bar capstone.
Play all seven function cells and explain the characteristic color.
Practice log
Date Module / mode Chord function D/U BPM Clean? Weak interval / resolution Next target
NEXT Level 68: E Phrygian dominant, diminished-seventh symmetry, altered dominant colors, and harmonic-minor improvisation synthesis.
Standard tuning. Fixed key: A harmonic minor. Mode names describe harmonic function, not seven unrelated box systems. Page 20 of 20

source_full_book_mastery.exact_full_page:
Guitar Exercises - Section VIII, Level 67
ADVANCE BY FUNCTIONAL HEARING, NOT MODE-NAME RECALL
Practice progression, error diagnosis, mastery gate, and log
THE MODE IS CORRECT ONLY WHEN THE CHORD AND RESOLUTION ARE AUDIBLE
Ten-phase practice progression Error diagnosis
1. P1 thirds, fourths, fifths, and sixths. 6. Seven mode-function cells. MODE NAME WITHOUT FUNCTION hold the chord or drone and stop on its root
INTERVAL RUN BECOMES SCALE remove the connecting notes; play only the pair
2. Translate each interval type through P2-P5. 7. Five i-iv-V7-i phrases.
AUG2 RUSH isolate F-G# and keep equal subdivisions
3. Seven triad overlays. 8. Three alternate progression families. V7 SOUNDS MINOR accent G# before adding F or C color
DIMINISHED CELL SOUNDS RANDOM state G#dim7, then resolve every voice
4. Seven seventh-chord overlays. 9. Five E Phrygian dominant cells.
III+ SOUNDS UNSTABLE land C-E-G# first; add B only after the triad is clear
5. Seven mode mirrors over sustained chords. 10. Characteristic resolutions and capstone. FORM LOSS return to quarter-note chord tones and name each bar
Mastery gate before Level 68
Play all twenty interval cells and identify the diatonic interval family by ear. Complete five i-iv-V7-i phrases and all three alternate progression families.
Spell and arpeggiate all seven triads and seven seventh chords. Perform E Phrygian dominant in five registers and resolve every cell to A minor.
Perform all seven mode mirrors while the local chord remains audible. Complete all five characteristic chord-resolution cells and the sixteen-bar capstone.
Play all seven function cells and explain the characteristic color.
Practice log
Date Module / mode Chord function D/U BPM Clean? Weak interval / resolution Next target
NEXT Level 68: E Phrygian dominant, diminished-seventh symmetry, altered dominant colors, and harmonic-minor improvisation synthesis.
Standard tuning. Fixed key: A harmonic minor. Mode names describe harmonic function, not seven unrelated box systems. Page 20 of 20

source_payload.pdf_region_text:
Guitar Exercises - Section X, Level 79
8 PASSES | 64 EVENTS
Module A - long-form dynamic arc and density architecture
DYNAMICS ARE A FORM SIGNAL, NOT A VOLUME KNOB APPLIED AT RANDOM
Bars Section Dynamic Density Register Instruction
1-4 Intro p 1-2 contacts/bar low leave maximum space
5-12 Verse A mp 4 contacts/bar low-mid steady comp; no fills until bar 8
13-16 Pre mf 4-6 contacts/bar middle rise register each bar
17-24 Chorus f 6-8 contacts/bar wide open voicings; short lead answers
25-32 Verse B mp 2-4 contacts/bar middle drop density immediately
33-40 Bridge mf -> f 4-7 contacts/bar middle-high build to second peak
41-44 Finale A f 6 contacts/bar high maintain energy
45-48 Finale B mf -> pp 4 -> 1 descending release into final tonic
Pass 1 uses only roots. Pass 2 uses shells. Pass 3 uses the full arrangement. If the dynamic contour disappears when note count is reduced, the arc is not yet internalized.
Complete-performance improvisation: long-form arcs, multi-key navigation, rhythmic displacement, cues, role changes, and ear-led recovery. Page 3 of 20

Visual nod: COMP -> LEAD. finish shell; sing next target; enter high register. Keep the current bar count.
Visual nod: LEAD -> COMP. resolve by beat 3; reform chord. Keep the current bar count.
Drum fill: COMP -> HIT. mute groove; match final ensemble hit. Keep the current bar count.
Held chord: LEAD -> SILENCE. resolve to guide tone; stop adding notes. Keep the current bar count.
Bass walk-up: COMP -> HIGH COMP. move to upper triad on next bar. Keep the current bar count.
Count cue: SILENCE -> LEAD. pre-hear beat-one target during count. Keep the current bar count.
Cutoff: ANY -> SILENCE. release pressure and mute. Keep the current bar count.
Extra bar: ANY -> MINIMAL. repeat one root/guide-tone idea only. Keep the current bar count.

Guitar Exercises - Section XI, Level 81
VOICE ORDER BEFORE FINGERING
Reference: compact, spread, diminished, and reduction vocabulary
NAME THE FOUR VOICES BEFORE CHOOSING A GRIP
Type Example Pitches low->high Primary use
Drop-2 Cmaj7 x 3 5 4 5 x C-G-B-E compact four-note melody/comp texture
Drop-2 G7 x 10 12 10 12 x G-D-F-B dominant with top-line third
Spread Cmaj7 8 x 9 9 8 x C-E-B-G bass separated from upper voices
Spread G7 3 x 3 4 3 x G-F-B-D root + guide tones + fifth
C#dim7 x 4 5 3 5 x C#-G-Bb-E passing connector to Dm7
G#dim7 x 11 12 10 12 x G#-D-F-B leading diminished into A minor
Reduction ladder
FULL: melody + upper guide + lower guide + bass The purpose of reduction is not to make the music easier permanently. It identifies which voice is
causing the breakdown while the form continues.
REDUCE 1: melody + one guide + bass
REDUCE 2: melody + bass
REDUCE 3: melody only
RESTORE: bass -> guide tone -> optional color

Guitar Exercises - Section X, Level 74
48 CONTACTS | 16 ACCENTS
Module A1 - three-note accent cycle across three bars
ACCENT EVERY 3 SIXTEENTHS; DO NOT RESTART AT THE BARLINE
Cell route: A3(C) - D2(E) - G0(G). Repeat the 3-note cell continuously. Accent the first note of every cell. The pitch cell and accent cycle return to beat 1 together after 3 complete bars.
Bar 1 of 3
Bar 1|1--e--&--a--2--e--&--a--3--e--&--a--4--e--&--a--|
Acc |>-------->-------->-------->-------->-------->--|
Grp |1--------2--------3--------4--------5--------6--|
Nte |C--E--G--C--E--G--C--E--G--C--E--G--C--E--G--C--|
Bar 2 of 3
Bar 2|1--e--&--a--2--e--&--a--3--e--&--a--4--e--&--a--|
Acc |------>-------->-------->-------->-------->-----|
Grp |------7--------8--------9--------10-------11----|
Nte |E--G--C--E--G--C--E--G--C--E--G--C--E--G--C--E--|
Bar 3 of 3
Bar 3|1--e--&--a--2--e--&--a--3--e--&--a--4--e--&--a--|
Acc |--->-------->-------->-------->-------->--------|
Grp |---12-------13-------14-------15-------16-------|
Nte |G--C--E--G--C--E--G--C--E--G--C--E--G--C--E--G--|

Standard tuning. Rhythm-first workbook: grouping, displacement, polyrhythm, and asymmetrical meter. Page 3 of 20

Module J — Section XI Completion Audit
Perform the 32-bar arrangement twice: first as the printed baseline, then as an alternate arrangement with at least six changed voicings/substitutions while the
melody and form remain unchanged.
Category 0 1 2
Melody clarity lost functional dominant
Bass independence lost functional confident
Guide-tone accuracy wrong mostly smooth
Reharmonization random plausible purposeful
Voice balance collapsed usable controlled
Dynamic architecture flat some contrast clear arc
Form/pulse lost recovers stable
Recovery restart simplifies seamless
Pass Section XI: 14/16 or better on two separate days, with no zero in melody clarity, bass independence, form/pulse, or recovery.
NEXT: Level 85 begins Section XII — Groove & Stylistic Rhythm. Fixed roadmap remains Levels 85–90 groove, 91–94 expression, 95–99 repertoire, 100–104
composition, 105 final capstone. HARD STOP after Level 105.

Guitar Exercises - Section XI, Level 82
8 FAILURE MODES | 64 EVENTS
Module J - recovery, reduction, and no-restart repair
RECOVER THE BASS DESTINATION FIRST, THEN REBUILD THE CHORD-MELODY TEXTURE
Failure Immediate repair Restore
Bass misses beat 1 play root only next bar restore walk one beat later
Melody disappears remove one inner voice keep bass + melody only
Chromatic approach sounds random state destination root first use only one approach note
Slash chord loses identity play upper chord separately re-add substituted bass
Bass and chord attack collide separate them by one eighth note recombine at slow tempo
Walking line outruns harmony reduce to quarter-note roots restore approach on beat 4
Hand cannot re-form chord end walk one beat early land destination shape cleanly
No-restart drill
Form lost bass roots only re-enter melody at next cadence
Intentionally miss one bass approach in every eight-bar run. Continue with roots only until the next cadence, then restore the walking line. The recovery is part of the exercise, not an interruption of it.
Walking-bass chord melody, chromatic approach bass lines, bass substitutions, independence, and longer solo-guitar arrangements. Page 19 of 20

MELODY MUST REMAIN SINGABLE WITHOUT THE CHORDS
Arrangement 1 - C major ballad
| Cmaj7 | Am7 | Dm7 | G7 |
Melody: E G A G | C B A G | F A G F | B A G D
Bass: C A D G
Bars 1-4: play melody + bass only. Bars 5-8: repeat the same phrase with guide tones and chord color added. Preserve melody rhythm exactly.
Reduction test Expansion test
Remove all inner voices. If melody + bass still communicate the form, the arrangement is structurally Add one extension only at cadence points: 9, 6, or 13. Reject any extension that masks the melody.
sound.
Final pass: perform once with hybrid picking and once with fingerstyle or pick-plus-middle/ring. Do not change tempo between methods.
Chord melody and independent-voice control: bass, inner guide tones, top-line melody, substitutions, and simultaneous accompaniment/lead. Page 13 of 20

Module E - Structural vs Incidental Classification
Detail Structural test
Chord inversion Does bass motion/function change?
Ghost note Does groove identity collapse without it?
Extension Does chord quality/voice-leading change?
Fill Does it cue a section?
Articulation Is phrase identity lost without it?
Tone/effect Does arrangement function survive clean?
Register Does moving it create masking or lose contrast?
Rest Does filling it damage groove/phrase?
Label each discovered detail S = structural, C = color, O = optional. Build the first performance using S only.

source_scope.pdf_excerpt:
Extended predominant chain | F#m7b5 | Bm7 | E7 | AmMaj7 |
Four quarter notes per bar.
Nte|F#--A---C---E---|B---D---F#--A---|E---G#--B---D---|A---C---E---G#--|
Deg|6---1---b3--5---|2---4---6---1---|5---7---2---4---|1---b3--5---7---|
Rol|>F#mF#m7F#m7F#m7|>Bm7Bm7-Bm7-Bm7-|>E7-E7--E7--E7--|>AmMAmMaAmMaAmMa|
e|----------------|----------------|----------------|----------------|
B|------------5---|----------------|----------------|--------5---9---|
G|--------5-------|----------------|--------4---7---|----5-----------|
D|----7-----------|------------7---|----6-----------|7---------------|
A|9---------------|--------9-------|7---------------|----------------|
E|----------------|7---10----------|----------------|----------------|
AUDIT Identify the pitch or chord quality that separates this progression from the preceding minor form.
Transformation passes
1. Keep beat 1 and change notes 2-4. 2. Convert the last three notes to shuffle eighths. 3. Use a symmetric melodic-minor descent. 4. Use a classical natural-minor descent only after the final tonic arrives.
5. Answer in a higher register.

Guitar Exercises - Section VI, Level 51
NEXT: MAJOR AND MINOR TRIADS
Practice progression, error repair, mastery gate, and log
ADVANCE WHEN THE SHAPE MOVES; DO NOT ADVANCE WHEN THE HAND ONLY SQUEEZES HARDER
Eleven-phase practice progression Error diagnosis
1. Root maps and silent calls DEAD BARRED STRING move index angle or height before squeezing
2. Pressure fade and release
DEAD CHORD-FINGER STRING curve the neighboring finger and move closer to fret
3. Partial-barre ladder
4. E-shape major family LOW E LEAK IN A SHAPE let index tip touch low E without pressing it
5. E-shape minor family
HIGH E DEAD IN A-MAJOR roll ring mini-barre away from high e
6. A-shape major family
7. A-shape minor family SOUNDING SHIFT release pressure fully before moving root fret
8. Quality and same-fret switches
9. Root ladders THUMB FATIGUE reduce clamp; use arm support and shorter voicing
10. Progressions and partial comping QUALITY ERROR isolate G-string or B-string quality note
11. Major and minor capstones
Mastery gate before Level 52
Find every natural root on low E and A strings; form all four movable families; perform clean low-to-high and high-to-low scans; switch major/minor quality at seven roots; transfer between same-fret E and A
families; play all four root ladders; complete the same-shape and mixed-shape progressions; perform both sixteen-bar capstones on two separate days; and finish every session without pain, numbness, or
lingering thumb tension.
Completion audit and practice log
root maps partial barres E major/minor A major/minor quality switches
same-fret pairs root ladders progressions partial comping capstones
Date Focus Root/shape BPM Clean? Weak string / movement Next target
Movable E-shape and A-shape major/minor barre chords. Use minimal pressure; stop for pain, numbness, or tingling. Page 20 of 20

Guitar Exercises - Section VI, Level 51
MINIMUM PRESSURE | NO DEATH GRIP
Barre pressure, index placement, and release mechanics
MOVE THE INDEX AND ARM BEFORE ADDING MORE THUMB PRESSURE
1. Place near the fret 2. Add arm support 3. Solve one dead string
The index lies just behind the fret wire. Roll slightly toward its Let the fretting arm draw the neck lightly toward the body Pick the failed string alone. Shift index angle or vertical
thumb-side edge. Avoid placing the soft center of every joint while the picking arm stabilizes the guitar. The thumb guides; position by a few millimeters. Do not respond by squeezing
directly over a string. it does not crush. every finger harder.
Pressure-fade cell Press-release pulse
Count|1--------2--------3--------4--------| Count|1----2----3----4----|1----2----3----4----|
Hand |PRESS----FADE-----BUZZ-----RESTORE--| Hand |P----R----P----R----|P----R----P----R----|
Pick |one string on every count | Sound|ring mute ring mute |ring mute ring mute |
Goal |restore only the pressure needed |
Use fret 5 first. Repeat on B and high e, then test the remaining strings. R means release pressure while keeping the index in contact. The thumb also relaxes.
Stop conditions
Normal effort can feel unfamiliar, but sharp pain, tingling, numbness, burning, or lingering hand tension is a stop signal. Shake out the hand, shorten the chord, move higher on the neck, or end the
session.
Movable E-shape and A-shape major/minor barre chords. Use minimal pressure; stop for pain, numbness, or tingling. Page 3 of 20

16 BARS | 128 EVENTS
Module I - sixteen-bar chord-melody capstone map
MELODY, BASS, GUIDE TONES, AND TEXTURE MUST REMAIN LEGIBLE THROUGH THE FULL FORM
Bar Chord Melody target Bass Function
1 Cmaj7 E C statement
2 Am7 C A answer
3 Dm7 F D rise
4 G7 B G cadence
5 Cmaj7 G C register lift
6 A7 C# A secondary dominant
7 Dm7 A D release
8 G7 F G turnaround
9 Em7 G E contrast
10 A7 C# A dominant
11 Dm7 F D predominant
12 G7 B G cadence
13 Cmaj7 E C return
14 Fmaj7 A F expansion
15 G7 D G final dominant
Each bar: beat 1 bass + chord body; beat 2 melody; beat 3 inner guide tone or dyad; beat 4 melody continuation or rest. Use fewer notes if independence breaks down.
16 Cmaj7 C C tonic close
Chord melody and independent-voice control: bass, inner guide tones, top-line melody, substitutions, and simultaneous accompaniment/lead. Page 17 of 20

5 PASSES | SAME 16-BAR FORM
Module I - capstone performance passes
ADD COMPLEXITY ONLY AFTER THE OUTER VOICES ARE INDEPENDENT
1. Melody only Sing first, then play top line alone.
2. Bass + melody No inner harmony. Keep both voices rhythmically independent.
3. Add guide tones Insert thirds/sevenths on beats 1 or 3 only.
4. Full chord melody Use complete voicings only where they do not hide melody.
5. Performance version Choose texture, dynamics, fills, and one substitution while preserving all structural targets.
Fail condition: melody disappears, bass timing shifts to accommodate the melody, or inner voices ring across a chord where they no longer belong.

Bar Chord Melody target Bass Function

ADD COMPLEXITY ONLY AFTER THE OUTER VOICES ARE INDEPENDENT
1. Melody only Sing first, then play top line alone.
2. Bass + melody No inner harmony. Keep both voices rhythmically independent.
3. Add guide tones Insert thirds/sevenths on beats 1 or 3 only.
4. Full chord melody Use complete voicings only where they do not hide melody.
5. Performance version Choose texture, dynamics, fills, and one substitution while preserving all structural targets.
Fail condition: melody disappears, bass timing shifts to accommodate the melody, or inner voices ring across a chord where they no longer belong.

Module I - Thirty-Two-Bar Expressive Texture Capstone
Bars Harmony Expression focus Dynamic
1-4 Am7-Dm7-E7-Am7 rakes + grace notes mp
5-8 A7-D7-A7-E7 double-stop slides mf
9-12 Cmaj7-Am7-Dm7-G7 natural harmonics + swells p
13-16 E5-G5-A5-E5 pinch harmonics f
17-20 Am7-E7-Am7-Am7 muted lead textures mf
21-24 G-D-Em-C mixed articulation chains mf -> f
25-28 Cmaj7-A7-Dm7-G7 swell/slide contrast mp
29-32 Am7-Dm7-E7-Am7 reduction and outro f -> pp
Pass 1: targets only. Pass 2: one articulation per bar. Pass 3: articulation chains. Pass 4: reduce density by 50% while preserving expression. Pass 5: record
one uninterrupted take.

Bars Section Harmony Groove role Guitar role
1-4 Intro Cmaj7-Am7-Dm7-G7 sparse roots/shells
5-12 Verse A Cmaj7-Am7-Dm7-G7 x2 steady pocket middle voicings
13-16 Pre Am7-D7-Gmaj7-D7 build rising register
17-24 Chorus Gmaj7-Cmaj7-Em7-D7 x2 open/full wide voicings
25-28 Bridge Em7-B7-Em7-A7 contrast reduced texture
29-32 Solo Dm7-G7-Cmaj7-A7 support + targets shells/lead
33-36 Final Chorus Gmaj7-Cmaj7-D7-Gmaj7 peak full arrangement
37-40 Outro Cmaj7-A7-Dm7-G7 release reduce to final target

restart maximum during early assembly; zero restarts on the final pass.

# Role Groove Key Energy Transition
1 Opener Rock E 4 clean stop -> count
2 Contrast Soul/R&B C 2 common-tone link
3 Lift Shuffle A 3 rhythmic handoff
4 Reset Minor ballad Am 1 full stop
5 Peak 1 Funk D 4 short texture bridge
6 Open section Jam-band G 3 medley-style link
7 Texture contrast Americana G 2 hard stop

Requirement Standard
Total duration approximately 25-30 minutes
Restarts 0
Unplanned dead time under 15 seconds total
Set list memory complete
Cold starts all 8 pieces
Designed transitions minimum 3
Dynamic arc at least one reset and two peaks
Injected failure recover without stopping set
Gear/patch changes executed within transition plan
Final ending clear and intentional

Module I - Forty-Eight-Bar Demo-Ready Arrangement Capstone
Bars Section Primary role Dynamic Density
1-4 Intro hook + texture p density 1
5-12 Verse groove foundation mp density 2
13-16 Pre rising register mf density 3
17-24 Chorus wide rhythm + hook f density 4
25-32 Verse 2 variation/counterline mp-mf density 2-3

41-44 Final chorus peak arrangement f density 4

Take one original composition from Level 100 or 101 and arrange it for at least three roles: foundation, harmony/groove, and hook/lead. Create both a full-band
version and a reduced one-guitar version.

Module I - Required Arrangement Deliverables
Deliverable Requirement
Form map all sections/bar counts
Role map who owns foundation/harmony/hook/lead
Register map low/mid/high assignment by section
Density map 1-5 by section
Bass map roots + important motion
Inner-voice map only structural guide/common tones
Groove map subdivision/note length/accents
Dynamic arc section levels and peaks
Solo handoff entry/exit plan
Reduction 50% density version
The arrangement is not complete until the reduced version still communicates the piece.
