instructions: 32 BARS | INTRO / VERSE / PRE / CHORUS / BRIDGE / OUTRO
Module I - thirty-two-bar full-song rhythm capstone: form and texture map
ONE COMPLETE TAKE; NO STOPPING BETWEEN SECTIONS
The capstone uses familiar open chords and five section-specific grooves. Memorize the form first. Speak the next section name during beat 4 of the final bar in the current section.
Section Bars Progression Texture Pattern contacts / bar
VERSE A 8 G | D | Em | C | G | D | C | D palm-muted 16th groove 8
PRE-CHORUS 4 Am | C | D | D increase register and dynamics 6
BRIDGE 4 Em | C | G | D half-time stop-time contrast 4
FINAL G 1 G one final attack; sustain 1
Speak section names and chord names while air-strumming. Do not fret the guitar until all 32 bars Use open chords in intro and chorus, palm-muted partials in verse, rising register in pre-chorus,
can be counted without a correction. stop-time in bridge, and a single sustained final G.
CAPSTONE CONTACTS 209 notated string contacts; the sixteenth-note air motion continues through every section.
Standard tuning. Sixteenth-note rhythm guitar, syncopation, dead strokes, releases, anticipations, and full-song comping. Page 16 of 20

DYNAMIC RULE Increase volume with velocity and register; do not deepen the pick or stiffen the wrist.

2. Muted strings only; reproduce all section grooves.

NO-STOP RULE A wrong chord does not stop the performance. Simplify to quarter notes and rejoin at the next barline.

Ten-phase practice progression Error diagnosis

HYBRID IMBALANCE reduce pick volume; shorten finger motion

Mastery gate before Level 64

source_session_duties.exact_text: Choose one crosspicking cell, one hybrid cell, and one sweep burst. Stop before fatigue changes the attack. Rest at least as long as the work interval during endurance training. A faster phrase is not successful if notes overlap, skipped strings ring, or the chord identity disappears.

steps.muting: Fretting hand releases the completed string. Picking-hand palm or spare fingers silence lower strings. The active note should be the only sustained pitch unless a printed pedal tone is intentional.
steps.same_string_sweep_reattacks: Preserve each printed D/U on the same string as an independent reattack. No continuous cross-string motion is inferred.
steps.source_rule: Each key receives ii-V-I-I. The harmonic route rises for ii-V-I and descends on the repeated tonic. Announce the next key during beat 4 of the tonic bar without changing the attack system early.

source_safety_setup.exact_text: Sweep and hybrid practice uses minimum pick depth and relaxed finger extension. Stop for pain or persistent tension.

source_volume_setup.exact_text: Reduce pick volume until m and a can match it comfortably. Do not solve a weak finger-plucked note by snapping the string or tensing the hand.

steps.stop_immediately: Pain, burning tension, uncontrolled string noise, or a collapsing pick grip ends the set immediately.

source.exact_text:
Guitar Exercises - Section VII, Level 63
REUSE THE CAPSTONES | NO EXTRA WRITTEN TONES
Full-performance orchestration, recovery, and phrase-shape control
THE PICKING SYSTEM SUPPORTS THE PHRASE; IT DOES NOT BECOME THE PHRASE
Four-pass orchestration Dynamic and density arc
1. One system for the complete capstone. Bars 1-4: p and sparse. Bars 5-8: mp with one repeated roll. Bars 9-12: mf with wider register.
Bars 13-15: f with one sweep climax. Bar 16: return to mp and release completely.
2. Printed four-system rotation.
3. Choose systems by register: pick low, hybrid middle, sweep high.
4. Choose systems by phrase job: crosspick question, hybrid answer, sweep climax.
Recovery cards Phrase-construction limits
Crosspick catches string -> simplify to three-note roll Use no more than two picking systems inside one four-bar phrase. Keep one recognizable
arpeggio contour. Land on a chord tone at every harmonic change. Leave at least one full-beat
Hybrid finger misses -> continue with pick-only target rest per four bars.
Sweep overlaps -> stop burst on highest clean note
Pick cycle lost -> use next target as new downstroke
Fatigue appears -> insert full-beat rest and reduce density
Final recorded assignment
Record one major and one minor sixteen-bar performance. The first take follows the printed systems. The second chooses systems by musical function. Evaluate tone equality, note separation, muting,
tempo, chord identity, dynamic shape, and recovery.
PASS The second performance must sound more musical, not merely more technically varied.

source_session_duties.exact_text: Choose one crosspicking cell, one hybrid cell, and one sweep burst. Stop before fatigue changes the attack. Rest at least as long as the work interval during endurance training. A faster phrase is not successful if notes overlap, skipped strings ring, or the chord identity disappears.

steps.muting: Fretting hand releases the completed string. Picking-hand palm or spare fingers silence lower strings. The active note should be the only sustained pitch unless a printed pedal tone is intentional.
steps.same_string_sweep_reattacks: Preserve each printed D/U on the same string as an independent reattack. No continuous cross-string motion is inferred.
steps.source_rule: The b5 of ii-m7b5, the major third of V7, and the minor third of i must remain audible while the system changes. The final tonic bar descends and resets the hand before the next key.

source_safety_setup.exact_text: Sweep and hybrid practice uses minimum pick depth and relaxed finger extension. Stop for pain or persistent tension.

source_volume_setup.exact_text: Reduce pick volume until m and a can match it comfortably. Do not solve a weak finger-plucked note by snapping the string or tensing the hand.

steps.stop_immediately: Pain, burning tension, uncontrolled string noise, or a collapsing pick grip ends the set immediately.

Bars Harmony Rhythmic task Contacts
1-3 Cmaj7 | Am7 | Dm7 group-of-3 sixteenth cycle; full 3-bar return 48

Performance passes Section-transition cues

Guitar Exercises - Section X, Level 74
RHYTHM FIRST | HARMONY SECOND
Practice progression, error diagnosis, and advancement
REPAIR THE EARLIEST RHYTHMIC LAYER THAT FAILED
Ten-phase progression Error diagnosis
1. Clap full group-of-3 cycle. ACCENT ADDS A NOTE return to even attacks and change volume only
2. Clap full group-of-5 cycle.
BARLINE MOVES tap quarters and speak bar numbers
3. Clap full group-of-7 cycle.
GROUP RESTARTS continue global event count across the barline
4. Add pitch cells without changing accents.
QUINTUPLET RUSHES practice one beat and land the next click
5. Complete eight metric displacements.
6. Play quintuplet and septuplet cells. SEPTUPLET COLLAPSES reduce tempo and accent only note 1
7. Separate and combine 3:2 voices.
POLYRHYTHM MERGES play each voice alone, then alternate
8. Separate and combine 4:3 voices.
ODD METER FEELS SHORT count large groups, not imaginary 4/4
9. Perform 5/4 and 7/8 studies.
DISPLACED MOTIF LOST sing the motif before moving its onset
10. Record the sixteen-bar capstone.
Advancement rules
Add 2 BPM after three clean complete cycles, not after one clean bar. For 5- and 7-group cycles, shorten to two bars only for diagnosis, then return to the full cycle. Increase quintuplet or septuplet tempo
only when the next quarter-note click remains exact.
Physical and musical boundary
Odd rhythm is not permission to tense the picking hand or over-accent every group. Use a small dynamic difference, preserve note length, and stop if the subdivision causes gripping or breath-holding.
Standard tuning. Rhythm-first workbook: grouping, displacement, polyrhythm, and asymmetrical meter. Page 19 of 20

Guitar Exercises - Section X, Level 75
120 CONTACTS
Module F - count-in, click reduction, and internal-time rehearsal
REMOVE EXTERNAL TIME SUPPORT IN STAGES
Pass Click Primary test Failure response
Pass 1 click every quarter establish form simplify rhythm, do not stop
Pass 2 click beats 2 and 4 backbeat stability simplify rhythm, do not stop
Pass 3 click beat 1 only barline stability simplify rhythm, do not stop
Pass 4 click every 2 bars phrase stability simplify rhythm, do not stop
Pass 5 click section starts only form memory simplify rhythm, do not stop
Pass 6 no click record and compare simplify rhythm, do not stop
Count-in protocol
Bar -2: listen only Do not use the count-in to discover the tempo. Hear the tempo internally before the count begins. The
first attack should confirm an already-established pulse.
Bar -1: count 1 2 3 4
Bar 1 : enter on planned attack
Section changes: internal count continues
Final bar: release together on planned subdivision
Level 75 - complete-performance integration. Standard tuning. Page 13 of 20

Module G - complete-performance rehearsal ladder
ADD COMPLEXITY ONLY AFTER THE FORM SURVIVES THE PREVIOUS PASS
Pass Material Primary test Advance when
1 Speak chart + tap pulse form no structural errors
2 Roots only harmony no structural errors
3 Shells / triads voice leading no structural errors
4 Written rhythm textures groove no structural errors
5 Cues + fills transitions no structural errors
6 Dynamics + register arrangement no structural errors
7 Lead / rhythm role changes orchestration no structural errors
T8hree-erroOr nhe iuenirnaterrrcuphteyd take performance no structural errors
1. Structural error: lost form, missed cue, stopped performance. Repair immediately. 2. Functional error: wrong chord quality, wrong section texture, missed target. Simplify until function returns. 3. Cosmetic
error: weak articulation or imperfect note. Continue and review after the take.
The rehearsal ladder is intentionally biased toward finishing. A complete imperfect take produces more useful diagnostic information than repeatedly restarting the first sixteen bars.

Guitar Exercises - Section X, Level 78
ADVANCE WHEN THE EAR PREDICTS BEFORE THE HAND MOVES
Practice progression, mastery gate, and Section X direction
LEVEL 78 IS PASSED BY PREDICTION AND RECOVERY, NOT BY SOLO DENSITY
Ten-phase progression Error diagnosis
1. Major pre-heard targets 6. Motif continuation
Target right after search -> sing earlier
Target wrong but chord right -> ear/function gap
2. Minor pre-heard targets 7. Comp -> lead
Cue missed -> phrase ended too late
3. Major guide lines 8. Lead -> comp
Form lost during lead -> reduce density
4. Minor guide lines 9. Random role cues
Comp re-entry late -> leave more silence
5. Phrase prediction 10. 16-bar capstone
Role switch unclear -> change register/texture
Mastery gate
Pre-hear and land all 24 major/minor targets with one decisive attack.
Sing both guide-tone voices through six major and six minor cadences.
Predict at least 10/12 phrase completions before seeing the answer.
Continue all eight motifs while preserving the requested identity variable.
Switch accompaniment -> lead and lead -> accompaniment on random cues without losing the bar count.
Next direction
Perform the 16-bar capstone at 28/32 or better on two separate days.
Level 79 will synthesize Section X into complete-performance improvisation: long-form dynamic arcs, multiple key centers, rhythmic displacement, ear-led recovery, ensemble cues, and a multi-chorus
performance designed to test the entire advanced integration layer.
The goal is a player who can hear, predict, support, answer, recover, and continue - without separating those actions into different practice worlds.
Ear-led improvisation: pre-heard targets, anticipatory guide tones, motif prediction, and accompaniment/lead role switching. Page 20 of 20

source_payload.pdf_region_text:
WHEN INDEPENDENCE FAILS, REMOVE A VOICE IN A FIXED ORDER
Melody hidden
Repair: remove extension
Then: keep melody + bass

txt_excerpt.text:
Melody hidden: remove extension; then keep melody + bass.
Bass late: remove inner voices; then play bass + melody only.
Chord change noisy: use shell voicing; then restore full grip later.
Top note missed: play melody alone next beat; then resume harmony after target.
Inner note sustains wrongly: release chord body; then let melody continue.
Right hand confused: return to bass-melody alternation; then rebuild pattern.
Substitution sounds wrong: restore original chord; then keep melody fixed.
Form lost: roots + melody target; then re-enter at cadence.

You are given only the following structural facts. All other arrangement decisions are yours.
Fact Supplied information
Length 24 bars
Tonal centers A minor, then C major
Required cadence E7 -> Am occurs before modulation
Required later cadence Dm7 -> G7 -> Cmaj7
Rhythmic identity one repeated 2-beat figure must recur
Lead identity one 4-note motif must recur in 3 registers
Ending must resolve clearly, not fade
Construct the form, chord sequence, groove, voicings, motif placement, transitions, dynamics, and recovery version. Then perform from memory.

source_payload.pdf_region_text:
Module J - Revision and Authorship Audit
Question Action
What is the piece's smallest recognizable identity? circle it
Which bar is weakest? rewrite only that bar first
Which note/chord is unnecessary? remove it
Where is the climax? make only that area strongest
Does bar 8 close or continue? choose intentionally
Can the piece survive 50% fewer notes? test reduction
Does it sound like an exercise? add contrast or asymmetry with purpose
Can you perform it from memory? if no, simplify identity
Pass Level 100: 14/16 or better across identity, development, harmony, melody/bass relationship, rhythm, form, revision, and performance. No zero in identity,
development, form, or performance.
Next: Level 101 develops larger form: A/B sections, verse/chorus contrast, bridges, transitions, thematic return, and 16-32 bar original composition.
Fixed roadmap: 100-104 Composition; 105 Final Musicianship Capstone. HARD STOP after Level 105.

Module J - Revision, Reduction, and Authorship Audit
Question Revision task
Does B contrast enough? change only one additional variable
Does bridge belong? restore one identity-bearing feature
Does return feel earned? improve bridge exit or reduce return
Where is the climax? remove competing peaks
Which transition is unnecessary? delete it and compare
Which section is too long? truncate without losing job
Can form survive 50% fewer notes? perform reduced version
Can you explain every section in one sentence? rewrite unclear section
Pass Level 101: 14/16 or better across identity, section contrast, bridge function, transition clarity, thematic return, form, revision, and performance. No zero in
identity, form, thematic return, or performance.
Next: Level 102 develops arrangement and orchestration for original music: multiple guitar roles, bass/inner-voice design, groove changes, dynamic
architecture, solo sections, and demo-ready 32-48 bar arrangements.
Fixed roadmap: Levels 100-104 Composition; Level 105 Final Musicianship Capstone. HARD STOP after Level 105.

source_payload.pdf_region_text:
Module J - Final 60-Minute Integrated Musicianship Examination
Block Minutes Task
1 0-8 Technique + fretboard reaction
2 8-16 Harmony + voicing + reharmonization
3 16-24 Groove/style switching
4 24-32 Ear/transcription reconstruction
5 32-40 Improvisation + expression
6 40-48 Repertoire adaptation + recovery
7 48-56 Original composition/arrangement performance
8 56-60 Reflection + final declaration
The exact minute count may shift slightly, but the entire exam should be completed in one session with minimal interruption.

Final Examination - Block 1: Technique and Fretboard
Minute Task
0-2 short warm-up + picking/legato control
2-4 random note/degree location
4-6 scale/arpeggio connection through two positions
6-8 bend/vibrato/harmonic/articulation accuracy
Score execution and immediate fretboard access equally.

Final Examination - Block 2: Harmony and Voicing
Minute Task
8-10 major ii-V-I in random key
10-12 minor iiø-V-i in random key
12-14 fixed top-note reharmonization
14-16 one secondary dominant + one passing diminished / pedal solution
Explain every non-diatonic chord before moving on.

Final Examination - Block 3: Groove and Style
Minute Task
16-18 straight rock -> funk
18-20 reggae/ska -> soul
20-22 country -> shuffle
22-24 interlock -> jam-band
Same tempo and harmony unless otherwise chosen. Style change must be audible without effects.

Final Examination - Block 4: Ear and Reconstruction
Minute Task
24-26 form/pulse from unfamiliar excerpt
26-28 bass/root map
28-30 harmony/groove
30-32 hook + functional performance
Do not spend the entire block chasing one uncertain extension.

Final Examination - Block 5: Improvisation and Expression
Minute Task
32-34 targets only
34-36 motif development
36-38 dynamic/expression arc
38-40 random cue: Return / Space / Build / End
One clear motif return and one clear ending are mandatory.

Final Examination - Block 6: Repertoire Adaptation
Minute Task
40-42 cold-start known piece
42-44 start from middle section
44-46 adapt section to new ensemble role/key
46-48 recover one injected failure and continue
A successful recovery is worth more than preserving a difficult but failing original part.

Final Examination - Block 7: Original Work
Minute Task
48-50 state identity/form of original
50-55 perform complete original or condensed core version
55-56 perform 50% reduction / alternate arrangement
The work must sound authored: identity, form, development, return, and ending.

Final Examination - Block 8: Reflection and Final Declaration
Question Answer in one sentence
What is your strongest domain?
What still needs specialization?
Which fallback saved the most performances?
Which technique do you now use less because you understand it better?
What is the next repertoire/composition goal?
What specialization track will you pursue, if any?
The core curriculum ends with self-directed musicianship. Future study should be chosen by musical goal, not by an arbitrary next level number.

select_register_repeat.instruction: After owned release, explicitly select the retained derived upper-octave repeat. These actual contacts are your chosen realization of the source register-repeat duty.

register_repeat.instruction: Perform both chosen upper-octave contacts in their original pair order as a complete repeat. Preserve both pitch roles and the written interval; keep form/pulse and resolve before the actual next harmonic landmark.
